# 05. Workflow execution

Status: current implementation.

Baseline: `56f0b397d0b313ec550791c1e2772525a9f7cf12`. Source review is static; no provider or device sessions were run.

## Boundary and layout

Three columns: admission at left, Temporal orchestration and three dispatch lanes across the center, plugin/provider work and durable results at right. Place the eligible sequential path in a lower inset, and a small dispatch-error exit beside TemporalExecutor.

## Exact components

- "Graph execution request" (client)
- "WorkflowService" (service)
- "Admission and routing" (service)
- "TemporalExecutor" (temporal)
- "MachinaWorkflow" (temporal)
- "Typed or legacy activity" (temporal)
- "AgentWorkflow" (temporal)
- "PiCodingAgentWorkflow" (temporal)
- "NodeExecutor" (service)
- "Registered plugin" (service)
- "Recorded model / tool operations" (temporal)
- "Providers and tools" (external)
- "Stored results and status" (state)
- "Eligible sequential execution" (service)
- "Error returned" (service)

## Exact directed relationships

- Graph execution request → WorkflowService
- WorkflowService → Admission and routing
- Admission and routing → TemporalExecutor [Temporal selected]
- TemporalExecutor → MachinaWorkflow
- MachinaWorkflow → Typed or legacy activity [frozen dispatch]
- MachinaWorkflow → AgentWorkflow [native agent]
- MachinaWorkflow → PiCodingAgentWorkflow [recorded Pi runtime]
- Typed or legacy activity → NodeExecutor
- NodeExecutor → Registered plugin
- Registered plugin → Providers and tools
- AgentWorkflow → Recorded model / tool operations
- PiCodingAgentWorkflow → Recorded model / tool operations
- Recorded model / tool operations → Providers and tools
- Registered plugin → Stored results and status [node outputs]
- Recorded model / tool operations → Stored results and status [recorded results]
- Admission and routing → Eligible sequential execution [eligible local path]
- Eligible sequential execution → NodeExecutor
- TemporalExecutor → Error returned [dispatch failure]

## Conditions and caveats

- Routing is frozen for a run; old histories retain their recorded dispatch.
- Redis parallel code is unreachable in shipped configurations.
- A Temporal dispatch failure returns an error; it does not rerun the graph locally.

# 06. Independent-node execution

Status: current implementation.

Baseline: `56f0b397d0b313ec550791c1e2772525a9f7cf12`. Source review is static; no provider or device sessions were run.

## Boundary and layout

Four clearly separated horizontal entry lanes, with no implication that one entry universally supports every node. Top: Canvas Run through WebSocket and WorkflowService into NodeExecutor for ordinary nodes, with a distinct new-Coding-Agent Pi workflow branch from WorkflowService to Activity or agent child. Second: graph admission into MachinaWorkflow with activity or agent-child dispatch. Third: agent tool call into the trusted connected-tool dispatcher and plugin boundary. Bottom: authenticated Workspace task through saved-node authorization/eligibility, durable controller, then invocation. Share only the registered-plugin destination where valid.

## Exact components

- "Canvas single-node Run" (client)
- "WebSocket handler" (service)
- "WorkflowService" (service)
- "NodeExecutor" (service)
- "Graph execution" (client)
- "MachinaWorkflow" (temporal)
- "Activity or agent child" (temporal)
- "Agent tool call" (client)
- "Trusted tool dispatch" (service)
- "Registered plugin boundary" (service)
- "Workspace task REST" (client)
- "Saved-node authorization" (service)
- "Workspace-task eligibility" (service)
- "WorkspaceTaskControllerWorkflow" (temporal)
- "NodeInvocationWorkflow" (temporal)

## Exact directed relationships

- Canvas single-node Run → WebSocket handler
- WebSocket handler → WorkflowService
- WorkflowService → NodeExecutor [ordinary nodes]
- WorkflowService → Activity or agent child [new Coding Agent: Pi workflow]
- NodeExecutor → Registered plugin boundary
- Graph execution → MachinaWorkflow [Temporal admission]
- MachinaWorkflow → Activity or agent child
- Activity or agent child → Registered plugin boundary [runtime-specific]
- Agent tool call → Trusted tool dispatch
- Trusted tool dispatch → Registered plugin boundary [connected tool scope]
- Workspace task REST → Saved-node authorization
- Saved-node authorization → Workspace-task eligibility
- Workspace-task eligibility → WorkspaceTaskControllerWorkflow [enabled and capable]
- WorkspaceTaskControllerWorkflow → NodeInvocationWorkflow [deduplicated submission]
- NodeInvocationWorkflow → Activity or agent child [recorded task dispatch]

## Conditions and caveats

- Independent does not mean every node accepts direct Workspace tasks.
- Saved-node identity, capability, graph connections and credentials remain prerequisites.
- Workspace submissions are epoch-fenced and deduplicated by their controller.

## Code evidence

- `server/routers/websocket.py` — handle_execute_node; saved graph context and WorkflowService admission; line 446 onward.
- `server/services/workflow.py` — WorkflowService.execute_node; lines 202–286, including native Pi admission.
- `server/services/handlers/tools.py` — execute_tool and _dispatch_tool; trusted configuration/connected tool scope.
- `server/services/node_invocations.py` — submit; authorization, workspace_task, enabled state, admission epoch and controller-owned deduplication; lines 167–275.
- `server/services/temporal/node_invocation.py` — NodeInvocationWorkflow; activity/native-agent/Pi dispatch.
- `server/services/temporal/workspace_tasks_workflow.py` — WorkspaceTaskControllerWorkflow; durable per-workflow submission control.

# Plugin and node contracts

Status: current implementation. Source baseline: `56f0b397d0b313ec550791c1e2772525a9f7cf12`.

## Components and boundaries

Show authoring/discovery on the left, registry/schema contract in the middle, two clearly separated outgoing lanes: UI catalogue→adapter→editor above, handler/typed-activity execution below. The capability index is a sidecar documentation output from metadata and class declarations/flags; it is not a NodeSpec consumer or runtime service. No node equals a separately deployed service.

- Recursive imports discover plugin modules. BaseNode subclasses register class, metadata, schemas and handlers; abstract kinds do not register as executable concrete nodes.
- NodeSpec assembles the backend/editor contract from actual metadata and schemas. Current frontend adapters consume the live contract.
- Handler-free configuration/context/visual nodes can still have catalogue metadata. Registration alone does not establish executable behavior.
- Typed Temporal activities and queues derive from declared plugin classes. Workflow-shaped agent/Pi dispatch and specialized task admissions have additional contracts.
- Workspace-task eligibility, trigger behavior, credentials and ownership prerequisites must be read per class. All registered types are documented in the companion index without claiming every type supports every admission.
- Unavailable twitterReceive stays marked unavailable; retired browserHarness belongs to migration/history notes, not the working registry graph.
- This is the current NodeSpec contract. The proposed frontend widget registry is a separate status-labeled view.

## Exact labels and relationships

- `modules`: **Node plugin modules** (service).
- `base`: **BaseNode registration** (service).
- `registry`: **Metadata + class registry** (service).
- `schemas`: **Input / output schemas** (service).

# 09. Teams and context

Status: current implementation.

Baseline: `56f0b397d0b313ec550791c1e2772525a9f7cf12`. Source review is static; no provider or device sessions were run.

## Boundary and layout

Main left-to-right loop: lead turn → Task Manager → durable task record → delegated workflow → connected teammate → persisted result → taskTrigger → lead review. Beneath this loop, put opt-in Context, explicit Memory and materialized Skills/Workspace as three separate resources with only their listed edges. Make the queued return a short feedback arrow from Task Manager to lead.

## Exact components

- "Lead agent turn" (service)
- "Task Manager" (service)
- "Durable task records" (state)
- "DelegatedTaskWorkflow" (temporal)
- "Connected teammate" (service)
- "Persisted task outcome" (state)
- "taskTrigger" (temporal)
- "Lead review and acceptance" (service)
- "Opt-in Context conversation" (state)
- "Explicit Memory tool" (service)
- "Skills and workspace files" (state)
- "Generation control" (temporal)

## Exact directed relationships

- Lead agent turn → Task Manager [assign_task]
- Task Manager → Durable task records [persist and queue]
- Task Manager → Lead agent turn [returns queued]
- Durable task records → DelegatedTaskWorkflow [Temporal execution]
- DelegatedTaskWorkflow → Connected teammate [authorized teammate]
- Connected teammate → Persisted task outcome
- Persisted task outcome → taskTrigger [terminal event after persistence]
- taskTrigger → Lead review and acceptance [new lead firing]
- Lead review and acceptance → Task Manager [accept / retry / finish]
- Opt-in Context conversation → Lead agent turn [load conversation]
- Lead agent turn → Opt-in Context conversation [save each turn]
- Opt-in Context conversation → Lead review and acceptance [continue same conversation]
- Lead agent turn → Explicit Memory tool [explicit remember / recall]
- Skills and workspace files → Lead agent turn [instructions and files]
- Skills and workspace files → Connected teammate [scoped workspace]
- Generation control → Durable task records [lifecycle admission]
- Generation control → Opt-in Context conversation [Reset uses new generation]

## Conditions and caveats

- Only agents connected to input-teammates can be assigned.
- Context is a plain conversation keyed by workflow, generation and agent node.
- Memory is an explicit tool; it does not automatically preserve conversation continuity.

# 10. Deployment and events

Status: current implementation.

Baseline: `56f0b397d0b313ec550791c1e2772525a9f7cf12`. Source review is static; no provider or device sessions were run.

## Boundary and layout

Three entry lanes across the top: verified push/webhook events, provider polling workflow, and Temporal Schedule/cron workflow, all leading to graph execution through their correct routes. In the lower half show durable generation/control and the lifecycle chain: Start→Running→Stopping/drain→Stopped→Resume→Running; Reset archives the generation and returns Ready, and a later Start creates a new generation. Keep event delivery and lifecycle controls visibly distinct.

## Exact components

- "Verified push / webhook" (external)
- "WorkflowEvent dispatch" (service)
- "Controller / trigger listener" (temporal)
- "Polling workflow and activity" (temporal)
- "Temporal Schedule and cron workflow" (temporal)
- "MachinaWorkflow" (temporal)
- "Generation and graph snapshot" (state)
- "WorkflowControlWorkflow" (temporal)
- "Start" (client)
- "Running" (service)
- "Stop gates new work" (client)
- "Drain admitted work" (temporal)
- "Stopped" (service)
- "Resume same continuation" (client)
- "Reset and archive" (client)
- "Ready for next Start" (service)

## Exact directed relationships

- Verified push / webhook → WorkflowEvent dispatch
- WorkflowEvent dispatch → Controller / trigger listener [Visibility and signals]
- Controller / trigger listener → MachinaWorkflow [admitted event]
- Polling workflow and activity → MachinaWorkflow [matching poll result]
- Temporal Schedule and cron workflow → MachinaWorkflow [scheduled run]
- Start → Generation and graph snapshot [allocate generation]
- Generation and graph snapshot → WorkflowControlWorkflow [snapshot and revision]
- WorkflowControlWorkflow → Controller / trigger listener [trigger lifecycle]
- WorkflowControlWorkflow → Polling workflow and activity [polling gates]
- WorkflowControlWorkflow → Temporal Schedule and cron workflow [pause / resume schedules]
- Start → Running [setup acknowledged]
- Running → Stop gates new work
- Stop gates new work → Drain admitted work
- Drain admitted work → Stopped [acknowledged drain]
- Stopped → Resume same continuation
- Resume same continuation → Running [same generation]
- Running → Reset and archive
- Stopped → Reset and archive
- Reset and archive → Ready for next Start [cancel resources and archive]
- Ready for next Start → Start [new generation]

## Conditions and caveats

- Current dispatch is fail-soft Visibility + signals, without a durable event inbox.
- Stop retains admitted work and buffered events; Resume releases the same continuation.
- Reset revision-guards cleanup and requires a later Start for the next generation.

## Code evidence

# 11. Approvals and external effects

Status: current implementation.

Baseline: `56f0b397d0b313ec550791c1e2772525a9f7cf12`. Source review is static; no provider or device sessions were run.

## Boundary and layout

Main path left to right: agent tool call→approval rules→allow/restrict or hold draft. The allowed branch has its own Allowed tool execution box which calls the external system and returns its result, bypassing the held-draft machinery. Hold leads through owner decision, Undo grace window, revision-fenced claim and one-attempt send to a three-outcome record. Add a dashed lower inset for implemented approval waiting, labeled rollout pending, which rejoins the same claim/send/outcome machinery. The ApprovalWorkflow wait and Implemented; rollout pending boxes and their edges must be dashed amber. Do not route every tool call through waiting.

## Exact components

- "Agent tool call" (service)
- "Approval rules and tool capability" (service)
- "Run or restrict" (service)
- "Allowed / restricted tool execution" (service)
- "Held approval draft" (state)
- "Owner decision" (client)
- "Undo grace window" (temporal)
- "Revision-fenced send claim" (state)
- "One-attempt tool activity" (temporal)
- "External side effect" (external)
- "sent / not_sent / unknown" (state)
- "Agent result or continuation" (service)
- "ApprovalWorkflow wait" (dormant)
- "Implemented; rollout pending" (dormant)

## Exact directed relationships

- Agent tool call → Approval rules and tool capability
- Approval rules and tool capability → Run or restrict [allowed / restricted]
- Run or restrict → Allowed / restricted tool execution [permitted call]
- Allowed / restricted tool execution → External side effect
- Allowed / restricted tool execution → Agent result or continuation [tool result]
- Approval rules and tool capability → Agent result or continuation [refused call]
- Approval rules and tool capability → Held approval draft [asked send]
- Held approval draft → Owner decision
- Owner decision → Undo grace window [Send]
- Undo grace window → Revision-fenced send claim [Undo window closes]
- Revision-fenced send claim → One-attempt tool activity [claim still valid]
- One-attempt tool activity → External side effect
- One-attempt tool activity → sent / not_sent / unknown [record outcome]
- sent / not_sent / unknown → Agent result or continuation
- Implemented; rollout pending → ApprovalWorkflow wait [versioned waiting path]
- Held approval draft → ApprovalWorkflow wait [when waiting is activated]
- Owner decision → ApprovalWorkflow wait [decision update]
- ApprovalWorkflow wait → Revision-fenced send claim [approved turn execution]

## Conditions and caveats

- Restricted tools still execute with enforced settings (`tool_calls._restricted` supplies restricted node data and arguments); only an explicitly refused call bypasses execution with a result.
- Ordinary new generations do not activate approval_wait_version at this baseline.
- Approval handling is capability/rule dependent; legacy in-process agents may refuse rather than hold.
- Approved sends are not automatically retried; interrupted attempts can have outcome unknown.

# Persistence and secrets

Status: current implementation. Source baseline: `56f0b397d0b313ec550791c1e2772525a9f7cf12`.

## Components and boundaries

Use three distinct regions: application persistence left, credential resolution center, runtime files right. Keep Application DB and Temporal history DB as separate cylinders with different owners. The separate credentials.db cylinder is encrypted; 1Password reference metadata lives in Application DB while secret values are fetched from external 1Password. Place workspaces, owner-local profiles and packages as distinct filesystem boxes. No arrows imply the model receives secrets or that every data store is encrypted.

- The resolved data root contains application SQLite, separate credentials.db, separate Temporal SQLite history, workflow workspaces, packages, daemon state and browser profiles. App PostgreSQL is supported when configured and required for distributed mode.
- Fernet field encryption protects local credential fields with a configured key. This does not establish encryption of application rows, filesystem contents or Temporal payload history.
- Saved 1Password enrollment/reference metadata is stored in application rows without secret values. Resolution reads the secret from the external source when needed.
- Distributed mode requires approved 1Password static-secret adapters and rejects unsupported OAuth/CLI-machine-local/inline credentials. Local credential behavior is not universally portable across replicas.
- Workspace identifiers/slugs and containment checks vary by handler; the diagram describes storage organization, not a universal sandbox guarantee. Known downloader/propagation limitations remain documented separately.
- Live browser profile/process state stays with its owner. Durable ownership metadata belongs to the shared application database, not the profile directory or credentials store.
- The optional external Gateway has its own state/credential plane. It does not replace the application database or credentials store.

## Exact labels and relationships

- `runtime`: **Application services / plugins** (service).
- `db`: **Application DB** (state).
- `history`: **Temporal history DB** (state).
- `temporal`: **Temporal server** (temporal).
- `auth`: **Credential resolution** (service).
- `credentials`: **Encrypted credentials.db** (state).
- `key`: **Configured encryption key** (state).
- `refs`: **Credential reference metadata** (state).
- `onepassword`: **1Password** (external).
- `workspace`: **Workflow workspaces** (state).
- `profiles`: **Owner-local browser profiles** (state).
- `packages`: **Managed packages / daemon state** (state).
- `external`: **Provider / integration APIs** (external).

- Application services / plugins → Application DB: application records.
- Application services / plugins → Temporal server: durable execution.
- Temporal server → Temporal history DB: workflow history.
- Application services / plugins → Credential resolution: resolve configured connection.
- Credential resolution → Encrypted credentials.db: read / write encrypted fields.
- Configured encryption key → Credential resolution: key derivation / decryption.
- Credential resolution → Credential reference metadata: binding lookup.
- Credential reference metadata → Application DB: metadata rows.
- Credential resolution → 1Password: resolve approved reference.
- Credential resolution → Application services / plugins: resolved credential.
- Application services / plugins → Provider / integration APIs: authenticated operation.
- Application services / plugins → Workflow workspaces: files / outputs / skills.
- Application services / plugins → Owner-local browser profiles: owned browser state.
- Application services / plugins → Managed packages / daemon state: managed runtime assets.

| [server/core/database.py](../../../server/core/database.py) | Application SQLModel/SQLAlchemy async engine. |
| [server/services/temporal/_runtime.py](../../../server/services/temporal/_runtime.py) | Separate Temporal CLI history database. |
| [server/core/encryption.py](../../../server/core/encryption.py) | EncryptionService field-level Fernet/PBKDF2 behavior. |
| [server/services/auth.py](../../../server/services/auth.py) | AuthService using separate CredentialsDatabase and credential-source resolution. |
| [server/services/credentials/sources.py](../../../server/services/credentials/sources.py) | CredentialSources metadata-only transactions. |

## Evidence

- RFC-0006 §§7, 11–16 and 22–24 amend admission, no owner-chat debounce, routing, parking, version flags and safety defaults; RFC-0007 amendments to RFC-0005 §17.5 distinguish approval activation from future gate migration.

- plugin_system.md phase rollout describes remaining PollingEventSource and DaemonEventSource migrations. GmailReceiveNode and EmailReceiveNode still subclass PollingTriggerNode; StripeListenSource already subclasses DaemonEventSource.

## Exact components

- **drivers**: Drivers / chat / webhooks — external.
- **verify**: Verify, cap, normalize, dedupe — proposed.
- **ingress**: Durable ingress / app DB commit — state.
- **ack**: Acknowledge producer — interface.
- **router**: DB router / subscriptions + sequence — proposed.
- **stream**: Conversation stream / deliveries + cursors — state.
- **relay**: Bounded relay / known workflow ID — proposed.
- **entity**: ConversationWorkflow / one turn at a time — proposed.
- **turn**: Turn child / Machina + agent execution — temporal.
- **history**: History + consumed cursor / atomic save — state.
- **outbox**: Durable outbox — state.

- **send**: Sender activity / sent, failed, unknown — proposed.

## Directed relationships

- **drivers → verify**: input.
- **verify → ingress**: append.
- **ingress → ack**: after commit.
- **ingress → router**: accepted rows.
- **router → stream**: route + sequence.
- **stream → relay**: pending batch.
- **relay → entity**: Signal-With-Start.
- **entity → turn**: admit one turn.
- **turn → history**: consume + persist.
- **history → stream**: advance consumed cursor.
- **turn → outbox**: enqueue effect.
- **outbox → gate**: eligible row.
- **gate → send**: permitted claim.
- **send → provider**: idempotent or at-most-once.
- **send → outbox**: record result.

## Boundaries and caveats

- The accepted roadmap is phased and unshipped as a complete data plane. Existing WorkflowEvent, graph and agent execution are reusable components, not proof of the proposed ingress guarantees.
- Signals are hints; app-database rows and cursors are authoritative in this target. A producer is acknowledged only after the durable ingress transaction commits.
- History save and consumed-cursor advancement are one proposed transaction. Unknown external outcomes require explicit resolution and are not silently resent.
- The migration strip describes current delivery → shadow comparison → durable sources → legacy retirement. The migration does not itself make unavailable twitterReceive functional.
- Cron remains Temporal Schedules, outside the EventSource class migration. The obsolete APScheduler source docstring is not a target architecture.

# 16. Parameter widget-registry proposal

Status: Planned — sketch.

**Status:** sketch. UNIMPLEMENTED SKETCH — DECISION PENDING.

Baseline: `56f0b397d0b313ec550791c1e2772525a9f7cf12`.

## Evidence

- frontend_architecture.md ParameterRenderer/current contract and Renderer registry shape sections explicitly distinguish the shipped switch renderer from the future colocated DIY registry sketch.
- get_node_spec and the backend NodeSpec adapter are already implemented. The client adapter consumes inputs, outputs, parameter schema and uiHints.
- Current ParameterRenderer.tsx dispatches on parameter.type in a large switch (baseline line 1298). The proposed components/inspector layout is absent.
- Current useParameterPanel.ts maintains editBuffer and originalParameters with useState; ParameterPanel passes controlled parameter values and onParameterChange. RHF + zod bindings belong to the future DIY registry sketch, not the current parameter editor.
- The documented sketch uses tester/rank dispatch with RHF + zod, inline scalar widgets, a recursive CollectionWidget and a CodeWidget. It preserves existing production interaction requirements.

## Source files

- [docs-internal/frontend_architecture.md](../../../docs-internal/frontend_architecture.md)
- [client/src/components/ParameterRenderer.tsx](../../../client/src/components/ParameterRenderer.tsx)
- [client/src/lib/nodeSpec.ts](../../../client/src/lib/nodeSpec.ts)
- [client/src/adapters/nodeSpecToDescription.ts](../../../client/src/adapters/nodeSpecToDescription.ts)
- [client/src/hooks/useParameterPanel.ts](../../../client/src/hooks/useParameterPanel.ts)
- [client/src/ParameterPanel.tsx](../../../client/src/ParameterPanel.tsx)

## Exact components

- **backend**: Backend NodeSpec / existing contract — current.
- **adapter**: NodeSpec adapter / existing — current.
- **switch**: Current switch renderer — current.
- **registry**: Proposed widget registry / tester + rank dispatch — proposed.
- **scalar**: Inline scalar widgets — proposed.
- **collection**: CollectionWidget / recursive collections — proposed.
- **code**: CodeWidget / editor wrapper — proposed.
- **buffer**: Local parameter edit buffer / existing — current.
- **form**: Proposed RHF + zod bindings — proposed.
- **save**: Existing save + node configuration — current.

## Directed relationships

- **backend → adapter**: schema + uiHints.
- **adapter → switch**: current path.
- **switch → buffer**: controlled values.
- **buffer → save**: save.
- **adapter → registry**: proposed dispatch.
- **registry → scalar**: match.
- **registry → collection**: match.
- **registry → code**: match.
- **scalar → form**: field binding.
- **collection → form**: field binding.
- **code → form**: field binding.
- **form → save**: save.

## Boundaries and caveats

- The registry is subject to a separate implementation decision. This image records the documented DIY preference without implementing the refactor.
- The current NodeSpec wire contract, backend precedence, adapter and controlled edit buffer are existing components, not future work. Proposed RHF + zod bindings must preserve the existing node configuration/save boundary.
- Credentials, uploads, drag/drop, expression behavior and save semantics are preserved interaction boundaries rather than newly invented widget APIs.
- JSON Forms, an alternate NodeSpec wire shape and VITE_USE_NODESPEC were superseded ideas. They are intentionally excluded.

## Visual review

Passed at native 1672 × 941 and documentation scale. Verified 10 unique components and 12 relationships. Current parameter editing uses the existing controlled useState buffer; RHF + zod bindings are explicitly proposed. Repeated save boxes are aliases of the same existing save/configuration boundary. Runtime-worker source cross-review found and corrected the initial form-state assumption. Two built-in ImageGen edits corrected colors/aliases and current-versus-proposed binding status; original generated artifacts are retained.

# Architecture and system design

Original generation baseline: `56f0b397d0b313ec550791c1e2772525a9f7cf12`. Audience: OpenCompany maintainers.

Current views were revalidated against public main `07e6d4c2c273c3693d2d0e3a84e04cdbafe68642`;
see the [public revalidation record](public-revalidation.json). The original generation baseline is preserved.

Twelve implemented-architecture views and four separately labeled proposal views share a dark visual style.
The PNGs were generated with built-in ImageGen, then checked against the editable Mermaid and source briefs.
Process, storage, ownership and status boundaries carry meaning; color alone does not establish guarantees.

[Node capability index](NODES.md) · [Registry data](nodes.json) · [Provenance catalogue](catalog.json) · [Review and validation](REVIEW.md)

| 14 | [Event OS control plane and resource lifecycle](14-event-os-control-plane-v1.png) | accepted-roadmap | [Mermaid](14-event-os-control-plane.mmd) · [Evidence](14-event-os-control-plane.brief.md) · [Prompt](14-event-os-control-plane.prompt.txt) |

| 16 | [Parameter widget-registry proposal](16-parameter-widget-registry-v1.png) | sketch | [Mermaid](16-parameter-widget-registry.mmd) · [Evidence](16-parameter-widget-registry.brief.md) · [Prompt](16-parameter-widget-registry.prompt.txt) |

## Reading the diagrams

- Local embedded SDK workers share the backend process; the local Temporal server is a separate child.
- Optional single-image Docker, desktop and development hosts are distinct from distributed deployment.
- Application state, Temporal history, secrets and live owner-local resources are separate boundaries.
- Graph runs, canvas Run, agent tools and direct Workspace tasks have different admission contracts.
- Live WebSocket delivery and the selected-frame worker relay do not provide a universal durable event bus.
- Approval waiting exists but ordinary new generations have not activated its AP.7 rollout.
- Node declaration/eligibility is not proof of successful provider, browser or device execution.

## Maintenance and validation

Each numbered bundle contains a PNG, `.mmd`, source brief, generation prompt and metadata record.
Targeted edit prompts and attempt records are retained. The catalogue hashes each selected asset.
Briefs record exact connections, prerequisites and known limitations; source evidence controls the review.

To update a view, review its implementation and status, edit its brief/Mermaid/prompt, generate with built-in
ImageGen, inspect the selected image at native and documentation width, and record the review and attempts.
After all sixteen views are reviewed, rebuild the catalogue:

```bash
python scripts/architecture_diagrams.py build-catalog
bun run docs:architecture:check
```

Run these commands at the repository root. Mermaid is parsed using the version already locked in
`bun.lock`, with the existing frontend test DOM; install the normal development dependencies first.
Python asset/navigation checks run in the CLI test job; live registry coverage runs in backend tests.
Image content requires human/source review in addition to structural checks.

Regenerate the capability snapshot with the backend Python environment from the repository root:

```bash
python scripts/architecture_diagrams.py export-nodes
```

The exporter reads declarations without executing nodes or contacting providers. Review runtime-source
changes against the pinned baseline before updating a diagram; its historical source SHA remains explicit.

## Earlier assets

Existing SVG and product-illustration URLs remain available in the [parent asset index](../README.md).
Outdated technical embeds now point to this suite. Product-specific references remain separately dated.

doc:docs/mobile-workspace.md.title: Mobile Workspace
doc:docs/mobile-workspace.md.content:
# Mobile Workspace

Mobile Workspace runs the open-source **mobile-use** agent against one persistent, local Android emulator. Mobile Agent and the Android tool are plugin nodes with a Workspace capability; its task execution uses the saved workflow, node configuration, and authenticated principal. The emulator belongs to the OpenCompany installation and is shared across Mobile nodes and workflows. Tasks queue for this device.

## Supported deployment

The initial implementation supports **Android on a Windows host**. The OpenCompany backend, Android SDK, emulator, device broker, and mobile worker must run on the same host. A remote browser can display the Workspace, but does not supply the emulator. Only the installation owner can access Mobile Workspace.

iOS is not enabled. Future iOS support requires a same-host macOS backend and Apple's simulator tooling; installing this plugin on Windows does not provide an iOS simulator. Physical devices, remote device farms, multiple concurrent emulators, and distributed mobile workers are outside this implementation.

The runtime singleton and its leases are process-local. Run one backend process with its local Temporal activity worker; multiple API processes or an independently deployed Android activity worker do not share this device broker. Merely placing separate processes on the same machine does not make their runtime state shared. A future multiprocess deployment needs a dedicated broker service and explicit authenticated routing to it.

## Setup and use

1. Install `uv` for the optional Python environment and enable the host virtualization support required by Android Emulator. Setup downloads pinned Android command-line tools and a private Temurin Java runtime when needed. An existing SDK can be selected with `ANDROID_SDK_ROOT` or `ANDROID_HOME`; the standard Windows Android SDK location is also detected.
2. Add **Mobile Agent** for direct tasks or employee delegation, or **Android** for an existing AI agent to call as a tool. Save the workflow and open **Workspace → Mobile**. The setup diagnostics inspect SDK tools, emulator acceleration, the system image, engine, and video server.
3. Review and accept the Android SDK license in setup. Setup installs the optional engine and Android packages and creates the persistent `OpenCompany` AVD using a Pixel 7 device profile. Network access and sufficient disk space are required for these downloads.
4. Click **Start phone**, which sits on the screen area, and wait for the phone's screen (**Starting phone…** shows beside the button until it appears). The emulator runs without a separate desktop window; the Workspace shows its video. Device storage persists across stopping and starting the emulator.
5. Click **Take over**, at the end of the phone's buttons, to sign in to the Play Store or install applications, or, in Dev mode, upload an APK under **Phone controls**. APK uploads are limited to 256 MB and require the current manual-control lease. Play Store availability comes from the selected Google Play system image; account sign-in is performed on the device.
6. Connect a provider in OpenCompany Settings, then choose a supported global model in the toolbar. Phone nodes use it by default. For an override, choose **Custom** under the node’s **Model selection**, or connect exactly one model to its **Model** input. Save the workflow. The resolved model is used for every mobile-use stage. OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemini credentials are supported. Choose a model with image input and tool use, then, in Dev mode, enter a request under **Ask AI to use the phone** and click **Run task**, or call the node through its agent connection.

The setup is optional. Ordinary application startup does not install the mobile engine or boot an emulator. Runtime data lives under the configured OpenCompany data directory's `mobile` subdirectory, including the engine environment, AVD, and device resource metadata. Stopping the emulator does not reset its apps or account sessions.

Setup shows the current component, download or SDK output, elapsed time, last update age, and recent activity. Complete compatible SDK packages are reused. Progress is saved in `mobile/setup-status.json`; reopening Workspace retains it. A backend shutdown or restart during setup is shown as interrupted with a retry action, rather than silently returning to idle. Retry reuses completed components; an incomplete download may need to restart. Setup does not continue while the backend is stopped. Timeout failures include the command and its latest output.

## Choosing a node

| Node | Use it for | Connection |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Mobile Agent** (`mobile_use_agent`) | Direct Workspace requests or delegated phone tasks | Global model by default; optional **Model** override; **Delegate** output for employee delegation |
| **Android** (`android_tool`) | Giving an existing AI agent a phone tool | **Tool** output into the agent’s **Tools** input; global model by default, with an optional **Model** override |

Both nodes use the same phone. Adding another node does not create another emulator. The existing `android_agent` and relay service nodes are separate integrations; they do not set up this local phone.

## Everyday controls

The live phone fills the available Workspace height in normal view, inside a phone frame (a dark bezel) shaped by the screen's own width and height, so it turns when the phone rotates; wide panels have side bars. Above it the server says which phone it is (`status.device`, "Pixel 7 · local emulator · up to 30 fps", from `DEVICE_NAME` and `VIDEO_MAX_FPS` in `_install.py`, which also set the AVD profile and scrcpy's `max_fps`). Below it the device bar has **Back**, **Home**, **Recent apps** and **Rotate** (on its side, and back), each sent through `/input` and enabled while you use the phone, and **Screenshot to Canvas** where the employee has a Canvas: `POST /screenshot` saves the screen as a PNG in the workflow's workspace (`write_media`, a read that needs no control) and `canvas_add` puts it on the board.

The phone tab (`MobileWorkspace`) is the same on Home and in the editor: setup, **Start phone** on the screen area while the phone is set up and off (with **Starting phone…** beside it while it boots), the phone and its device bar, **Type on phone** while you hold the phone, and a **Help & diagnostics** disclosure at the tab's foot. Dev mode (`MobileWorkspace dev`) adds **Full view** in the device bar, the AI activity panel, **Ask AI to use the phone**, and **Phone controls** (Stop phone, refresh, APK installation while you hold the phone, setup history): on Home the employee does the phone's AI work, and the Workspace's status pill shows their latest step. Stopping the phone is done from Dev mode.

**Take over**, at the end of the device bar while you do not hold the phone, takes the phone's lease and stops a running employee, on Home and in the editor alike. (It is the Workspace dock's button, passed to the phone view as `action`. A host that passes none gets the view's own Take over and Hand back there, which take and release the lease and stop no one.) **Hand back**, in the Workspace's "You're in control" banner, releases the lease with `resume: true`, so a task waiting for you goes on; when this view no longer holds the lease (it was hidden meanwhile), `POST /resume` lets a waiting task go on without it. A hidden view lets go of the lease, so Take over shows in the device bar again and takes it back without stopping the employee twice. `/resume` is refused while someone uses the phone and does nothing when no task of that workflow waits: the phone is shared, so one employee's Hand back never lets another employee's task go on. Each action an AI task takes on the phone ("Tapped the screen", "Went back"; `TASK_STEPS` and `KEY_STEPS` in `_runtime.py`), and you taking the phone over and handing it back, adds a line to the employee's Workspace step log (`services/workspace_steps.py`), whose newest shows on the Workspace's status pill while they work; a line never holds typed text or what the screen showed.

In Dev mode, expand **Ask AI to use the phone** to enter a task; collapsing it keeps your draft. The **Phone controls** section under it holds Stop phone, refresh, APK installation while you hold the phone and completed setup history, and says what the phone is busy with.

In Dev mode, choose **Full view** in the device bar to fill the screen. The task panel, AI activity and Phone controls are hidden meanwhile. The device bar stays outside the picture, so it does not cover Android buttons. Use **Exit full view** or **Esc** to return. Entering full view keeps the current connection and does not restart the phone or grant manual control. The Browser view has the same button in its row of page controls. If the browser does not support fullscreen, use the Workspace's Expand button instead.

| Label | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Start phone** | The phone is installed but needs to be started before tasks can run. |
| **Starting phone…** | Android and its automation connection are initializing. Wait for the phone's screen. |
| **Take over** | Pause AI control and use the screen yourself. The Workspace's Take over also stops a running employee. |
| **Hand back** | Release manual control and resume a waiting task from the current screen. In the Workspace it sits in the "You're in control" banner, and resumes the employee. |
| **Stop phone** | Dev mode, under **Phone controls**: shut down the phone while preserving apps and sign-ins. Cancel an active task first. |

The labels are the same on Home and in the editor. Hiding the phone's view releases manual control without resuming a waiting task.

Connection warnings clear after a successful status check. Action errors have a **Dismiss** button. Task submission is disabled while the phone is off. Download details, completed setup history, and technical diagnostics are collapsed by default.

## Model selection

Both Mobile Agent and Android use this order:

1. A connected **Model** node overrides all node/global settings. Multiple connections or a disabled/invalid connector produce an error rather than falling back silently.
2. With **Model selection = custom**, the saved phone provider/model is used. An empty model uses that provider’s configured default.
3. With **Model selection = global** (the default), the current toolbar selection is read for every new task. Changing it applies to the next task, not a worker already running.

The selected model serves every mobile-use stage. OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini are supported. An unsupported or missing global selection gives an actionable error; it never silently selects a different provider. Credentials always come from stored provider settings. Android’s AI-visible tool schema remains prompt-only, so an agent cannot override model selection or saved execution limits through tool arguments.

Gemini backend selection follows the main AI agent: Vertex AI Express credentials use Vertex, and Developer API credentials use the Gemini Developer API. The isolated phone worker receives an explicit backend setting derived from the stored credential; it does not inherit an unrelated host setting. Terminal events include `model_backend=vertex_express` or `model_backend=gemini_developer`, without printing the credential. A rejected Android tool result is shown as a failed node, even though the handled error is returned to its calling AI agent.

OpenAI and Anthropic (Claude) use their own saved API credentials and official SDK endpoints by default. A saved OpenAI or Anthropic custom endpoint is passed unchanged to the phone engine, matching the main agent's provider configuration. All three model-selection modes support these providers. Choose a model that supports image input and tool use; a valid API key alone does not establish access to every model. Endpoint values and credentials are excluded from diagnostic logs. Client construction is verified with the installed engine SDKs; this does not constitute a live provider-generation test.

## Runtime files and Git

`mobile_root()` currently resolves a relative `DATA_DIR` against the backend process’s working directory. With source development launched from `server/` and `DATA_DIR=.opencompany`, the installed phone is therefore under `server/.opencompany/mobile/`. This differs from the application’s canonical repository-relative data resolver. An absolute `DATA_DIR` avoids this ambiguity. Do not move an existing installation or switch its data directory while the backend is running.

The repository ignores `server/.opencompany/`. Emulator disks, snapshots, downloaded dependencies and logs are runtime data, not source changes; deleting them is not Git cleanup. Preserve `avd/` to retain the phone’s apps and sign-ins. Test fixtures and research checkouts under `.tmp/` can be removed once their checks finish.

## Control and task lifecycle

### Android tool for AI agents

Add the **Android** tool node (`android_tool`) and connect its **Tool** output to an AI agent's **Tools** input. The tool follows the saved global model by default. Optionally choose a custom model in its settings or connect an OpenAI, Anthropic, or Gemini model node to Android’s **Model** input; a connected model takes priority. Save the workflow, then set up and start the phone in Workspace → Mobile. The agent calls `android` with one argument, `prompt`, such as “Open Settings and turn on dark mode.” The tool uses the same mobile-use engine, owner checks, task queue, manual takeover, and saved time/step limits as Mobile Agent. It does not install software or accept licenses automatically.

### Troubleshooting and logs

Workspace shows plain-language phone status and clears connection warnings after a successful status check. **Take over** enables manual interaction; **Hand back** returns control to a waiting task. Technical checks and recent events are under **Help & diagnostics**.

Operational events are written to `mobile/mobile.log` relative to the active data directory, rotating at 1 MiB with three backups. They include startup, driver/video failures, task lifecycle and command durations. Errors include exception type, error code where available, and stack locations. Prompts, typed text, screenshots, credentials, and command parameters are excluded. Existing emulator output remains in `mobile/emulator.log`.

| Symptom | Check or recovery |
| --- | --- |
| Setup appears slow | Expand download details and recent setup activity; large system images take time. Complete compatible SDK packages are reused. |
| Setup interrupted after a backend restart | Use **Retry setup** after accepting the SDK terms. Completed components are reused; partial downloads may restart. |
| Phone will not start | Open **Help & diagnostics** for the acceleration check, then inspect `mobile/mobile.log` and `mobile/emulator.log`. |
| `readuntil() called while another coroutine is already waiting` during startup | Older code let status polling read the driver’s initialization pipe concurrently. The fix shares `driver_lock` across initialization and commands and skips geometry polling during lifecycle transitions. Restart the backend after updating. |
| Phone works but an old error remains | Current UI clears recovered connection warnings; dismiss action errors. Refresh the frontend after updating. |
| New Android node is absent | Restart the backend to register the plugin and refresh the frontend. Search for **Android**, type `android_tool`. |
| Task asks for a model | Select a supported global model, choose a custom provider/model in the phone’s settings, or connect a model to the phone’s **Model** input. A parent agent’s separate custom model is not inherited automatically. |
| Live view cannot connect | Check recent video events. Only one viewer is supported; close another preview and use **Reconnect**. |

`setup-status.json` retains setup progress across backend restarts. Recent diagnostic events in status are bounded to 40 records in memory; `mobile.log` and its rotated backups retain operational history on disk. Logs exclude user content, but still include workflow/run identifiers: review them before sharing. The startup race explains a failed request and phone cleanup; it does not by itself prove a whole-backend crash.

Video is a read-only scrcpy transport. Mouse, touch, text, navigation, rotation, APK installation, and agent mutations go through the server's device-control broker rather than the video socket. The initial preview supports one browser tab at a time.

Taking control revokes the agent's lease and capability before stopping its worker, then waits for an already admitted device mutation to drain. A monotonically increasing epoch rejects delayed inputs from an old controller. Operation identifiers deduplicate successful mutations within the current lease. An uncertain device failure fences control and requires recovery rather than replaying the mutation automatically.

Resuming starts a fresh agent worker against the current device state with a new capability. This is not continuation of an in-memory model conversation. The remaining active time and step budgets are carried forward. A task can wait for human control for up to 30 minutes. Cancelling a queued task prevents it from starting; cancelling a task while a person controls the device preserves that person's lease.

Workspace submissions use a client-generated submission UUID and a durable Temporal workflow identity scoped to principal, saved workflow, and node. Repeating a submission returns the existing task; reusing its UUID with a different prompt is rejected. Mobile task activities have automatic retries disabled. This is not a guarantee that arbitrary device actions are globally exactly-once across host failure.

### Resetting phone tasks

Use the workflow toolbar's **Reset** for phone tasks submitted through **Ask AI to use the phone**, as well as phone work invoked by the workflow. Direct Workspace submissions are tracked by a per-workflow Temporal `WorkspaceTaskControllerWorkflow`, so Reset is available even when the regular workflow has never started.

Reset blocks new Workspace submissions, cancels queued and running tasks for this workflow, and waits for cancellation and phone cleanup before reporting completion. Other workflows' phone tasks are unaffected. If cleanup or Temporal status is unavailable, Reset remains unconfirmed and can be retried; an already-ready workflow alone is not proof that its phone task stopped. The workflow remains stopped afterward.

The phone stays running, with its apps, sign-ins, and existing human-control lease preserved. Reset clears this workflow's task and activity panel and browser submission recovery IDs, then loads a fresh phone status. If you were controlling the phone, choose **Take over** again to reconnect this view's manual controls. Completed task history remains in Temporal.

After upgrading to this implementation, restart the backend and its Temporal worker so they register `WorkspaceTaskControllerWorkflow` and its cleanup activity. The process-local device broker still requires the backend and mobile activity worker to share the supported single-process deployment described above.

## Engine isolation and credentials

OpenCompany installs mobile-use into its own Python 3.12 environment. The main server does not import its agent dependencies. Each task receives a separate worker process; a trusted device process owns the explicitly selected emulator serial. The worker's injected controller talks to a loopback capability broker. It does not choose an ADB serial or receive an arbitrary host-command API.

A maintained source patch injects the controller before mobile-use's normal device initialization and redirects screenshot and platform-helper calls. It blocks SDK-side app installation and disables dotenv loading. The patch fails closed when its expected source structure changes. The upstream SDK's cancellation method alone is not used as proof that device work has stopped.

The node resolves the selected provider's existing default-account credentials on the server and passes only that provider credential in the worker configuration. Credentials are not supplied by the browser and are not included in task status. Device processes receive a filtered environment. Agent telemetry and trace recording are disabled by this integration. Task screenshots and prompts still go to the configured model provider as part of inference. Custom provider base URLs are not currently exposed by the Mobile Agent configuration.

## Dependency pins and attribution

The optional installer verifies downloaded artifacts before extraction or execution:

| Component | Pin |
| --- | --- |
| mobile-use source | `62913c933e21b27da353a89316a09f60525af496` |
| Source archive SHA-256 | `e2bac1f1d47e895d8c9ec840b0e896391ffd664ed2d4149a1ff1744252ca8384` |
| Python dependencies | Upstream lockfile, installed with `uv sync --frozen --no-dev` |
| scrcpy server | `4.1` |
| scrcpy artifact SHA-256 | `deacb991ed2509715160ffdc7907e47b4160eb30d1566217e9047fd5b8850cae` |
| Android command-line tools | Windows revision `15859902` |
| Command-line tools SHA-256 | `90ae805d20434428bffcb699c290860f19bb5f66a67e6b330067e3de801fb04a` |
| Private Java runtime | Temurin JRE Windows x64 `21.0.12.1+1` |
| Java archive SHA-256 | `d35f31e712f0fcf6ac5a093edc90204fbff22f720ba3950bd09d331d5e621636` |
| Android system image | `system-images;android-36;google_apis_playstore;x86_64` |

The Android package identifier selects an SDK package, not an immutable revision checksum. Updating the engine pin requires reviewing the patch, its bypass coverage, and the upstream lockfile together. Source archive extraction preserves upstream legal files; mobile-use is Apache-2.0 licensed, and its attribution and NOTICE must remain with redistribution.

## Local integration versus Minitap services

[mobile-use](https://github.com/minitap-ai/mobile-use) is the open-source Python agent and CLI reused here. The embedded preview, lease broker, takeover behavior, optional installation, and Workspace task routing are OpenCompany integration code.

Minitap's [platform](https://www.minitap.ai/platform#slack-cli-mcp) and [miniTest documentation](https://www.minitap.ai/docs/minitest) describe separate hosted testing products, including managed runs and integrations. This local plugin does not automatically provide their device fleet, hosted test reports, Slack integration, or hosted MCP service, and does not require a Minitap account for local engine execution.

## Validation and limitations

Android tool calls publish live step counts and phases to the normal canvas node-status channel and the AI activity panel of Dev mode's Workspace, including calls made by another AI agent. These are internal phone steps; the parent agent advances its own turn when the tool finishes. Step counts retain the already-consumed budget after manual takeover/resume. Model waits are labelled separately from device work. The Android tool's registered `android-phone-skill` teaches goal-based calls, manual handoff, and error handling; existing workflows can add it through their Master Skill node, while new tool connections use the normal auto-add-skill policy.

Manual control avoids an extra geometry/status round trip after every input. Device geometry uses the automation server's current display dimensions, falling back to the SDK size query when missing; taps and swipes still validate current size and rotation before executing. Non-coordinate commands avoid unnecessary geometry reads, and status polling does not queue behind a busy driver. Device read/action timings remain in Terminal to distinguish device latency from model inference time. These changes do not eliminate the phone engine's multiple model calls per task.

Android lifecycle and task events appear in the application's **Terminal** under source `mobile`, prefixed `Android:`. They are also retained in the bounded `mobile.log` and Workspace's recent phone activity. For task debugging, look for `engine_starting`, `engine_stage`, `engine_failed`, and `engine_exited`; correlate them by execution ID, run ID, workflow, and node. Model events include the selected provider/model and failures include the HTTP status and engine stage. HTTP 400 means the provider rejected the request, 401/403 indicates credentials or permissions, 404 indicates a missing model, 429 indicates quota/rate limits, and 5xx indicates a provider service failure. Invalid-key responses reported as HTTP 400 are classified as authentication failures.

Raw engine stderr and provider response bodies are not forwarded because they can contain prompts, phone screenshots, or API keys. The structured worker protocol supplies diagnostic metadata instead. Earlier generic `ClientError` failures cannot be reconstructed from logs that discarded this metadata; restart the backend after updating, then retry the task to capture a diagnostic event. This logging does not include a continuous Android OS `logcat` stream.

Phone startup first checks for an existing emulator. Recovery requires the console-reported AVD path to match this installation and the process to belong to its Android SDK. A process-wide device lock prevents two updated backends from owning the same writable phone. A disconnected automation driver can be restarted without launching a second emulator. Stop waits for the emulator and cleans up its owned child processes; it does not wipe phone data or stop unrelated emulators.

If startup fails, the message remains in Workspace after a refresh. A duplicate-AVD error means another emulator still holds the phone; if verified reconnection is unavailable, close that OpenCompany emulator and retry. Do not delete AVD lock files or use `-read-only` to bypass ownership. `emulator.log` retains launcher output and rotates to `emulator.previous.log` before a new launch when it exceeds 2 MiB. Error classification reads only the current attempt; `mobile.log` records recovery and boot-probe timeout events without model prompts or credentials.

Run backend validation with a boolean `DEBUG` environment value (for example, `$env:DEBUG='false'` in PowerShell). Values such as `release` fail settings validation in subprocess tests. Source-boundary checks exclude installed runtime data in `.opencompany` and legacy `.machina`; the mobile engine runs in its own dependency environment. The Android tool intentionally receives canvas edges to resolve its connected model, and the device driver's JSON wire replies are protocol output rather than application logs.

Automated tests exercise fencing, successful-operation deduplication, cancellation while draining, takeover and resume with fake subprocesses, queued cancellation, source-patch compatibility, and Python syntax compilation of the patched upstream package. Additional tests use the actual loopback HTTP broker with a fake driver, reject unsafe archives and checksum mismatches, and verify that SDK tools run through Java arguments without a command shell. Patch tests require `.tmp/mobile-use-upstream` or `MOBILE_USE_UPSTREAM_SOURCE` pointing to the pinned checkout; they skip when that fixture is absent.

An earlier local smoke test executed `worker.main` profile construction, SDK initialization, a fake task, and cleanup using the actual pinned dependency environment in `.tmp/engine-smoke` and a fake controller. It made no model request and connected to no emulator.

A separate Windows host check confirmed usable WHPX acceleration, a real Android boot, a 1080 × 2400 automation connection, and screenshot/UI inspection, followed by clean shutdown. That sequential check did not cover concurrent Workspace polling; dedicated regression tests now cover the startup race. The temporary smoke-test fixtures were removed after use.

Automated tests also cover the Android tool’s schema and saved execution limits, privacy-filtered bounded diagnostic logging, setup interruption recovery, and connection-warning recovery in the UI. These checks do not establish successful Play Store login, APK execution, live model inference, or a complete browser-video acceptance run. Validate those on a supported Windows host before treating this as production device automation. Current task results contain a response and run identity; the artifact list is empty, and hosted-style videos or reports are not generated.

## Planned iOS implementation

This is an implementation plan, not currently supported functionality. Keep the Workspace capability, task submission, ownership checks, and lease protocol shared, and add platform-specific lifecycle, driver, installation, and video adapters.

1. Add a macOS-only setup diagnostic for Xcode selection, accepted Apple licenses, installed simulator runtimes, and the chosen simulator device type. Setup must ask for the required Apple license acceptance and must not promise unattended Xcode installation.
2. Create or select one managed simulator by persisted UDID using `xcrun simctl`; explicitly boot it, wait for readiness, and shut down only the simulator owned by this installation. Never infer the target from whichever simulator happens to be booted. Preserve simulator data across normal restarts.
3. Implement an iOS driver in a separate trusted process on the same Mac. Evaluate and pin the upstream simulator controller's IDB companion requirements. Route its screenshots, hierarchy reads, gestures, text, app lifecycle, and platform helpers through the same lease checks as Android. Do not allow the agent worker to discover devices or spawn its own companion.
4. Add a simulator video adapter with a defined framing and geometry contract. Android scrcpy is not an iOS transport. Validate encoding, browser decoding, rotation, coordinate scaling, disconnect cleanup, and backpressure on the supported macOS and browser versions before enabling live preview.
5. Accept simulator-compatible application builds and install them through a lease-protected `simctl` operation. Do not describe arbitrary physical-device IPA files or iOS App Store installation as supported simulator workflows. Display platform-specific app prerequisites and controls.
6. Extend the pinned upstream patch and smoke tests for the iOS context, then execute the acceptance matrix below on a real Mac. Keep the iOS Workspace entry disabled until the lifecycle, automation, and takeover checks pass together.

## Acceptance matrix

| Area | Automated coverage now | Required device acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Setup | Checksums, archive safety, license refusal, Java argument boundary | Clean Windows x64 setup, acceleration diagnostics, SDK download failure and retry |
| Agent adapter | Pinned-source patch compilation and real-dependency fake-task smoke | Image-capable model completes a task through the broker |
| Device lifecycle | Runtime tests use fake processes | Start, stop, crash, restart, persistent apps and session state |
| Ownership | Lease fencing, drain, deduplication, queue cancellation, scoped identities | Two browser tabs, delayed input, takeover during a real device mutation |
| Human resume | Fake subprocess termination and new capability | Agent resumes from the manually changed screen within remaining budgets |
| Video and input | Transport code is separate from mutation broker | H.264 decoding, rotation, scaled pointer coordinates, typing, disconnect cleanup |
| Android apps | APK admission and installation are broker-owned | Install a simulator-compatible APK; manually authenticate and install from Play Store |
| iOS | Not implemented | Same-Mac lifecycle, IDB adapter, simulator app install, preview, gestures, fenced takeover |

Passing a source or fake-process test does not count as passing the corresponding device acceptance check.


### Live Android activity

Dev mode's Workspace shows the active phone task's model/provider, step budget, total elapsed time,
current phase duration, and time since the last reported activity (Home leaves this panel out). The main activity panel
shows the SDK's subtask plan and current subtask, followed by the latest 40 plan/action
updates. Actions include the selected app or screen target, the SDK tool's explicit intent,
duration, and confirmed tool outcome. A tool completing an action does not mark a subtask
complete: subtask status comes from the SDK's planner/orchestrator updates. Interrupted
actions whose outcomes were not confirmed are shown as unconfirmed.

The counter is labeled **Engine step** because it measures LangGraph execution steps,
including planning and coordination, rather than taps or completed subtasks. Nested chain
callbacks and graph branches at the same step do not generate duplicate counter events.
The current subtask stays visible across model waits and device reads. A resumed worker
creates a fresh plan from the current screen; earlier activity remains in the timeline.

A separate collapsed **Technical activity** section retains the latest 40 phase/device
events: model requests/responses, screen/accessibility-tree reads, and device operations.
Consecutive identical phase messages are coalesced. Completed operations include duration.
The last task remains visible after completion, failure, or cancellation until another task
runs; history is in memory and clears on restart. Older runs cannot recover details that
were not captured at the time.

A 30-second quiet period shows a notice, not a claim that the engine is stuck. Use the last
phase to distinguish a model wait from device I/O; take manual control using Take over if needed.
The panel is outside the phone canvas and hidden in full-screen mode. Detailed summaries
are bounded and available only through the owner-only mobile status response. They can
contain task-specific plan descriptions and screen labels. Typed tool payloads and input
tools' echoed field contents are omitted, and URL strings are redacted. These summaries
are not sent to diagnostic logs or the generic workflow status broadcast. Raw model
responses, provider thinking blocks, cumulative agent thoughts, screenshots, and injected
graph state are never forwarded to the activity panel.

This integration follows the SDK's [Agent configuration](https://www.minitap.ai/docs/mobile-use-sdk/sdk-reference/agent)
and the pinned source's `AgentConfigBuilder.with_graph_config_callbacks(...)`: graph node
results expose `subgoal_plan`, and tool callbacks expose intent/arguments plus
`Command.update.executor_messages` with `ToolMessage.status`. The SDK's internal
`on_plan_changes` hook is not exposed by this pinned Agent configuration. No additional
upstream patch or dependency is needed. [Local trace recording](https://www.minitap.ai/docs/mobile-use-sdk/core-concepts/observability)
is a separate feature that creates screenshots and step artifacts; `record_trace=False`
remains intentional for the live activity panel.

Regression coverage includes callback filtering, SDK-shaped plans, tool error results,
input-content filtering, interruption, bounded histories, and preserving subtask context
during quiet waits. An optional test executes a mock graph with the installed pinned SDK
and its real executor tool node, without a model request or device connection.
