| `claude/`, `whatsapp/` | Claude Code login, WhatsApp session |
| `home/` | `$HOME`: gh, stripe and cf logins, bun and uv caches (Codex uses `/data/codex`) |

`opencompany.env` holds `API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, the key that decrypts `credentials.db`. Back the two up together and keep the file private. If the key changes, stored credentials can no longer be decrypted.

An image that pins a new Temporal server minor (`server/config/temporal_cli.json`) deletes `temporal.db` and the old CLI on its first start. Every deployment then shows Failed, and its owner resets and starts it (see [TEMPORAL_ARCHITECTURE.md](./TEMPORAL_ARCHITECTURE.md#server-management)).

Back up `/data` while the container is stopped. `workflow.db` and `temporal.db` run in SQLite's WAL mode, so recent commits live in a `-wal` file next to each until SQLite folds them back in: a copy taken while the app runs needs the `-wal` and `-shm` files too, and a `-wal` file must never be deleted. SQLite needs working file locks, so keep `/data` on the named volume or a local disk, never NFS or SMB.

## Configuration

Settings resolve in this order, the later one winning: `.env.template` (baked into the image), then `/data/opencompany.env`, then the container environment (`environment:` in `docker-compose.yml`). To change a setting, add a `KEY=value` line to `/data/opencompany.env` or an entry under `environment:`, then restart the container.

A secret you pass under `environment:` before the first start is written into `/data/opencompany.env` instead of a random one, so removing it from `docker-compose.yml` later changes nothing.

The image sets these on top of the template:

| Variable | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `DATA_DIR` | `/data` | All state on the volume |
| `OPENCOMPANY_ENV_FILE` | `/data/opencompany.env` | Secrets and your settings on the volume |
| `HOME` | `/data/home` | CLI logins and caches survive upgrades |
| `DEPLOYMENT_MODE` | `self_hosted` | Server posture: full Temporal concurrency, API docs not public |
| `VITE_AUTH_ENABLED` | `true` | Login required |
| `NODEJS_EXECUTOR_HOST` | `127.0.0.1` | The code sidecar binds IPv4 loopback, which exists even where container IPv6 is off |
| `NODEJS_USER_PACKAGES_DIR` | `/data/nodejs-user-packages` | Packages installed for code nodes persist |
| `BROWSER_RUNTIME` | `system` | Use the image's installed browser; no testing-browser fallback |
| `BROWSER_FAMILY` | `chromium` | Discover Chromium supplied by the browser extra through PATH |
| `BROWSER_HEADLESS` | `true` | Render inside the workspace without a desktop window |
| `PYTHONUNBUFFERED` | `1` | Log lines reach `docker compose logs` as they are written |

**Browser runtime configuration:** the Dockerfile sets `BROWSER_RUNTIME=system`, `BROWSER_FAMILY=chromium` and `BROWSER_HEADLESS=true` in every image, not only with the browser extra; without that extra there is no Chromium, so a Browser node fails clearly instead of downloading one. These are the image defaults; compose `environment:` can override them. The headless image setting matches the application default: render in the workspace without a desktop window. Chromium is resolved through PATH at startup; the image does not pin an executable path. The former `AGENT_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH` has been removed from the Dockerfile and is not read by this runtime. `BROWSER_RUNTIME=testing` is the only mode that downloads pinned Chrome for Testing; it is never a missing-browser fallback. Validate the built image and Linux libraries before deployment.

The image has no Node. It links `/usr/local/bin/node` to bun, so the plugin CLIs whose entry scripts start `#!/usr/bin/env node` (vercel, cf) run on bun, as in the official oven/bun images. Browser automation installs browser-use through uv instead.

With the `browser` extra: Chrome refuses to run as root with its sandbox on, so the image adds `--no-sandbox` through a drop-in, `/etc/chromium.d/no-sandbox`. Debian's launcher reads flags only from that directory and ignores a `CHROMIUM_FLAGS` environment variable. Debian's own `dev-shm` drop-in already adds `--disable-dev-shm-usage` when Docker's `/dev/shm` is small.

Those drop-ins apply to Debian's Chromium launcher. OpenCompany supplies its runtime launch flags and detects sandbox/shared-memory constraints. The image already sets `BROWSER_HEADLESS=true` for displayless operation; do not rely on the former agent-browser/Xvfb startup path.

Leave `HOST` and `PORT` at their template values. The backend uses `HOST` to reach itself; the published bind comes from the entrypoint's `--host 0.0.0.0`. `PORT` is repeated in the Dockerfile's `EXPOSE` and the compose mapping, which do not follow a change made in `/data/opencompany.env`. Publish only the app port: the WhatsApp bridge and Temporal listen on internal ports without authentication, and the code sidecar's `/health` answers anyone (it runs code only for requests carrying the token the backend started it with).

### Serving other machines

Compose publishes the app on `127.0.0.1` only, so only this machine reaches it. To serve other machines, drop the `127.0.0.1:` prefix from the `ports:` mapping, put a TLS proxy in front, and set `JWT_COOKIE_SECURE=true`. Until you do, the log warns at every start that the session cookie travels over plain HTTP.

The proxy should also refuse `/ws/internal`. That is where the backend's Temporal workers call back in; it skips the login check and runs any node a message names, `shell` included. The handshake requires a token derived from `SECRET_KEY` (see [authentication.md](./authentication.md)), and the workers reach it inside the container, so blocking it at the proxy costs nothing and adds a second layer. Keep `Host` intact through the proxy, or list the public origin in `CORS_ORIGINS`: every WebSocket handshake refuses an `Origin` that is neither the request's own host nor listed there. Compose keeps the `127.0.0.1` mapping by default to limit exposure to this machine. The image enables login; register the owner before exposing it through a proxy.

## Upgrading

```bash
git pull
docker compose up -d --build
```

The volume keeps state, including downloaded tools in `/data/packages`. Refresh behavior belongs to each installer: version-aware installers, such as Cloudflare's, replace a cached tool when its pinned version changes. Follow the specific tool's diagnostics before removing a cache directory; removing all packages is not a required upgrade step.

## Stopping

`docker compose stop` gives the backend up to 120 seconds to drain its Temporal workers and record a clean shutdown. If the container is killed before that, the next start treats it as a crash and pauses the running deployments; resume them from the canvas.

With plain `docker run`, pass `--init` and `--stop-timeout 120` to get the same behaviour.

## Limitations

- **Temporal Web UI.** The dev server binds loopback inside the container, so its UI is not reachable from outside.
- **CLI login.** Claude Code's browser callback targets the container's localhost. Log in from an interactive shell in the container (`docker compose exec opencompany sh`) with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/data/claude` set, or supply `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` through `environment:`. For Codex, use device authentication in the credentials panel. A manual login must use the app-managed CLI with `CODEX_HOME=/data/codex`, for example `CODEX_HOME=/data/codex /data/packages/node_modules/.bin/codex login --device-auth` after the app has installed it. Native browser login requires the browser to reach the backend's localhost callback. See [Codex headless authentication](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth#login-on-headless-devices).
- **Owner-checked panels under login.** New workflows created through the REST save route receive placeholder owner `owner` rather than the logged-in account. REST updates preserve an existing workflow's owner. The Canvas, Memory, Context and dataSource panels check that owner, so they can refuse the logged-in user for a newly placeholder-owned workflow. This identity-propagation limitation is separate from legacy rows with empty ownership. `company deploy` VMs, which also require a login, behave the same.
- **Browser image integration.** The image selects system Chromium with `BROWSER_FAMILY=chromium` and enables `BROWSER_HEADLESS=true` for displayless operation. The default system mode fails clearly when no installed browser exists. Testing mode is a separate opt-in download. Both modes install the pinned browser-use CLI with uv. Validate selected-browser version/profile compatibility and Linux libraries in the built image; adding the extra alone is not an end-to-end browser check.
- **Agent nodes need the `git` extra and a git repository.** Claude Code and Codex agents work in git worktrees, and the image contains no `.git`. Run `git init` in a workflow's workspace and make a first commit before pointing an agent at it. Set a commit identity once from a shell in the container (`git config --global user.name ...` and `user.email ...`); it is stored in `/data/home` and survives upgrades.
- **Bind mounts.** A bind mount works in place of the named volume, but the Temporal CLI is then downloaded on first start (a new named volume receives the copy baked into the image), and the directory must allow executables, symlinks and Unix sockets. Prefer the named volume on Windows and macOS hosts.
- **Memory.** Give the container at least 1 GB. At idle the backend holds about 180 MB of process memory and the Temporal dev server about 115 MB; `docker stats` shows up to about 450 MiB because it also counts the page cache of the code they run.
- **Disk.** The image is about 1.3 GB, and the `browser` extra adds about 1.2 GB. A build needs room for its layers on top of that. On Docker Desktop they land on the drive that holds Docker's disk image, which is C: on Windows unless you move it (Settings > Resources > Advanced > Disk image location). A build that fills that drive makes Docker's filesystem read-only and takes down every running container.
- Built and tested on linux/amd64.

## Optional external services

- Redis: `REDIS_ENABLED=true` and `REDIS_URL=redis://<host>:6379`.
- A Temporal cluster: `TEMPORAL_SERVER_ADDRESS=<host>:7233`. With a non-loopback address the backend connects to it instead of spawning its own dev server.

## Maintaining the image

No CI job builds the image. What keeps it in step with the rest of the repo:

- **Toolchain pins.** The `oven/bun` tag must match the root `package.json` `packageManager` (what CI's setup-bun reads), and the `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv` tag must match `desktop/runtimes.json` (the desktop bundle). `test_docker_image_pins_match_the_bun_and_uv_pins` in `cli/tests/test_release_pipeline_config.py` fails when one moves without the other.
- **The port.** `EXPOSE` and the container side of the compose mapping repeat `PORT` from `.env.template`; `test_docker_port_matches_the_template_port` in the same file fails when the template changes without them.
- **Line endings.** `.gitattributes` pins LF for `*.sh` and `docker/Dockerfile`, so a Windows checkout builds the same image. A CRLF entrypoint fails under `sh` at the first line.
- **The build context.** Docker does not read `.gitignore`. When you add a local state directory or a secret file pattern to `.gitignore`, add it to `.dockerignore` too, or `COPY . .` bakes it into the image.
- **Build steps.** The build stage runs the same two commands as CI (`bun install --frozen-lockfile`, `bun run build`), then `uv sync --frozen --no-dev --extra docs`: the committed `server/uv.lock`, without the contributor tools, with the `docs` extra `company build` also installs. A new build step belongs in `company build`, not in the Dockerfile, so every channel gets it. Step `[6/6]` fetches the Temporal CLI into `DATA_DIR`, which is why a new named volume starts with it.
- **The runtime file list.** The runtime stage copies only what `core/approot.py` reads: `server/`, `client/dist`, `.env.template`, `package.json`, `.opencompany/workflows` and the entrypoint. A new path the backend reads outside `server/` needs a `COPY` line there.
- **Optional tools.** A system package that only some nodes need goes into an `EXTRAS` entry, not the default image.

## Why the container doesn't run `company serve`

`company serve` needs the CLI's own venv and the root `node_modules`, and reads only `<app>/.env` (it ignores `OPENCOMPANY_ENV_FILE`). Its supervisor would also add a second shutdown deadline: it tree-kills the backend after `backend_shutdown_grace_seconds` (`cli/_common.py`; 125 s with the template's Temporal settings), independently of compose's `stop_grace_period`. The entrypoint runs the uvicorn command the desktop shell uses instead; see [desktop_host_contract.md](./desktop_host_contract.md) for the backend's side of that contract.

doc:docs-internal/DOCUMENTATION_AUDIT.md.title: Documentation and supported-node audit
doc:docs-internal/DOCUMENTATION_AUDIT.md.content:
# Documentation and supported-node audit

**Baseline:** committed `56d4154e713845d93124875b271144acac8d26cd`, reviewed on 2026-11-02 in an isolated worktree. Earlier investigation used older commits; findings here were rechecked against this baseline. Uncommitted changes in the main checkout were excluded.

This audit corrects documentation and shipped skill defaults and adds offline documentation checks. It does not change product APIs, node schemas, runtime flags or execution behavior. Stored user/project skill overrides remain authoritative.

## Coverage and method

The baseline contains 413 tracked Markdown files. Every document is classified in the [corpus inventory](audits/MARKDOWN_COVERAGE.md); implementation evidence and review boundaries are recorded in these ledgers:

- [Reference docs](audits/REFERENCE_DOCS.md): runtime, UI/desktop, security, workspace and design/reference material.
- [Operations docs](audits/OPERATIONS_DOCS.md): setup, CLI, deployment, integrations and entrypoints.
- [Core nodes](audits/CORE_NODES.md): core node types, every declared operation, selector branches, shared execution paths and core skills.
- [Integration nodes](audits/INTEGRATION_NODES.md): 69 integration types and their complete declared operation/selector inventory, plus integration and role skills.

The runtime registry reconciles 157 node types at this baseline. Counts are observations, not fixed test targets. The registry gate also checks metadata/spec/handler relationships and discovery failures. `twitterReceive` is registered but explicitly unavailable; retired `browserHarness` is a migration card, not another working implementation.

Direct canvas Run, graph execution, agent-tool calls, controlled Temporal runs and specialized Workspace tasks are assessed separately. Independence from employee teams does not remove graph, credential, runtime, ownership or connection prerequisites. A hidden Run button or agent-shaped renderer does not establish backend capability.

Shared contracts are reviewed once and each node's overrides are recorded. Dynamic MCP, SDK, CLI and named-provider dispatch are audited as adapter contracts and built-in presets; arbitrary remote servers and future upstream operations are not claimed verified.

The two `SKILL.v1.md` files are active, opt-in Browser/Process defaults selected by `services/skill_defaults.py`. They preserve legacy defaults and user overrides; they are not historical snapshots.

## Corrections

| Area | Result |
|---|---|
| Employee lifecycle | Safe Apply preserves conversations, accepted work and paused state; Reset and explicit interruption are documented separately. |
| Runtime and models | Bounded delegation, actual snake_case fields, Pi dispatch, fallback prerequisites, activity-specific retry/timeout behavior and disabled rollout flags are explicit. |
| Security | REST placeholder ownership and JWT deactivation limitations are described accurately; per-call 1Password capability is separated from gateway integration limitations. |
| Shipped skills | Removed Memory tools/transcript assumptions, unsupported Python imports/state/exception names, process input, scraper/search/proxy/HTTP arguments, Apify inputs, Twitter reply IDs and Maps callable/schema examples were corrected. |
| Integration behavior | WhatsApp URL media sources, quote/vCard fields and flat send results; trigger waiting/polling versus deployment; current email poll setup; Maps implementation limitations are explicit. |
| UI and desktop | Mixed REST/WebSocket transport and polling, remote close-code reconnect behavior, client commands, AppShell ownership, NodeSpec flags and live theme authority are corrected. |
| Setup and deployment | GCP enables required Temporal; native LLM credentials use supported sources; Docker login/cache/ownership guidance and current CI/Pi build descriptions are reconciled. |
| Status and navigation | Three missing node cards were added, the node index regenerated, active links repaired, and current/planned/dormant/prototype/history boundaries clarified. Retired Docker instructions are preserved verbatim in the archive. |

## Separate code findings

These are implementation observations, not fixes supplied by this documentation change. Source inspection is distinguished from runtime proof in the linked ledgers.

| Finding | Current evidence / follow-up |
|---|---|
| Account deactivation does not reliably revoke unexpired API/WS access | Main admission boundaries verify JWT claims; active-account lookup is stronger on auth/status routes. Add boundary-level HTTP/WS and already-connected-socket tests before changing revocation behavior. |
| New REST workflow ownership uses placeholder owner | Existing owners are preserved; new rows can disagree with numeric authenticated principals. Identity propagation needs a separate product change. |
| Nearby Places schema/service mismatch | Params declares latitude/longitude/place_type, while the helper reads lat/lng/type and can use fallback coordinates/type; keyword also follows an incompatible options path. Documentation warns against presenting those results as the requested location. |
| Maps saved-key propagation | Params drops the executor-injected api_key before the Maps service reads it; the runtime Google Maps setting can mask a saved-credential-only failure. This affects the three Maps nodes and requires a separate credential-boundary fix. |
| Standalone chat-model settings | Several declared tuning fields are not forwarded by AIService.execute_chat; thinking_enabled with a nullable thinking_budget can raise int(None). Provider capability does not establish that this standalone path forwards every schema option. |
| Downloader/chunker service fields differ from Params | Some legacy camelCase lookups ignore configured snake_case values. Existing cards now make those operational limitations explicit; changing behavior needs targeted regression tests. |
| Downloader path and response-size boundary | The service decodes a URL basename before joining it to output_dir without containment checking, and does not cap response bytes. Treat this as a separate security/reliability code finding; the docs do not claim safe bounded downloading. |
| RLM limits are service-only fields | The service reads limit/depth/budget/timeout options that the specialized node's Params discards. The documentation no longer promises that those node settings are configurable. |

Earlier Reset/job cleanup findings from the initial investigation are resolved in this committed baseline; they are not repeated as open defects.

## Drift prevention

Existing CLI/backend test jobs now cover real registry/card completeness, index freshness, tracked Markdown links/images/anchors, implementation source paths, skill metadata and selected executable examples. Unknown example fields are checked before permissive schema validation where the contract forbids them; documented extension fields remain supported.

Checks make no HTTP requests. They preserve historical bodies, validate incoming/current-successor navigation, and use narrow, explained exceptions for proposed paths, templates and optional sibling checkouts. A structural pass does not prove every semantic claim.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Core node suites | 540 passed, 2 skipped across the isolated offline core suites, including job-source, Mobile and cron coverage. |
| Integration node suites | 673 passed across 15 offline integration suites: 667 in the isolated full run plus 6 import probes rerun with DEBUG=false after an inherited host value of release caused Settings parsing failures. The first sandbox run was inconclusive after Windows temporary-directory access failures. |
| Documentation/parser/index checks | 884 passed: Markdown navigation/source paths, parser fixtures, package-aware commands and index freshness. |
| Plugin/skill contracts | 162 passed: plugin/NodeSpec/skill contracts, active v1 defaults and user-override preservation. |
| Embedded documentation | 13 passed: temporary-manifest packaging, Agent Builder docs and restricted Python examples (including proxy formatting). |
| Historical Docker extraction | Body preserved verbatim; baseline/extracted body hashes match. |

No paid-provider calls, real OAuth/vault access, browser/mobile sessions, cloud provisioning, visual fidelity benchmarks or live deployment acceptance were performed. External vendor guarantees, arbitrary SDK/MCP operations and real hardware behavior remain explicitly unverified. The audit is a code-backed static review supplemented by offline tests.

doc:docs-internal/dodo_payments_service..title: Dodo Payments Service
doc:docs-internal/dodo_payments_service..content:
# Dodo Payments Service

Self-contained plugin at [`server/nodes/dodo_payments/`](../server/nodes/dodo_payments/)
over the official **Dodo Payments Python SDK** (`dodopayments`, a server
dependency, generated by Stainless from Dodo's OpenAPI spec). Two nodes in the
`payments` palette group, beside Stripe:

- `dodoPaymentsAction` (workflow node + AI tool `dodo_payments_action`): typed
  operations for the everyday flows (payments, subscriptions, customers,
  products, refunds, disputes, checkout and customer-portal links), `call` for
  any other SDK method, and `list_operations` to discover them.
- `dodoPaymentsReceive`: a trigger that fires on each verified webhook
  delivery to `/webhook/dodo-payments`, on a canvas Run and deployed.

**Auth model: an API key in OpenCompany's encrypted store, plus the mode it
belongs to.** A Dodo key works only in the mode it was created in
(test.dodopayments.com or live.dodopayments.com) and carries no marker saying
which. `DodoPaymentsCredential` (`ApiKeyCredential`, id `dodo_payments`) keeps
three rows: the key under the provider id (the field the modal validates),
`dodo_payments_mode`, and the optional `dodo_payments_webhook_key`
(`extra_fields`). Validation asks `GET /brands` in test mode, then live mode
(`_sdk.key_mode`; every business has a brand, and the route requires the key),
and the credential's `validate` override saves the mode that accepted it. The
owner never types the mode; a key stored without one makes the node answer
with the `PermissionDeniedError` envelope asking to validate it again.

**No ambient configuration.** Every client is created with the key and the
mode's base URL (`dodopayments.ENVIRONMENTS`) passed explicitly, so
`DODO_PAYMENTS_API_KEY` or `DODO_PAYMENTS_BASE_URL` in the server environment
never authenticates a node or points it elsewhere.

## File map

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `__init__.py` | Registers the webhook source, the canary trigger type, both output schemas and the `dodoPaymentsEndpoints` dropdown loader; both nodes auto-register on import |
| `dodo_payments_action.py` | `DodoPaymentsActionNode(ActionNode)`, `usable_as_tool=True`, `tool_name="dodo_payments_action"`, both canvas handles kept visible, eighteen `@Operation`s, the `ApprovalSpec`; `_run` resolves the credential before any work |
| `dodo_payments_receive.py` | `DodoPaymentsReceiveNode(WebhookTriggerNode)`: `event_type` set to the envelope type, `build_filter` on `data["event_type"]`, `_check_precondition`, `shape_output` returning `event.data` |
| `_sdk.py` | Every SDK touch, imported lazily: `open_client`, `key_mode`, the endpoint index (`endpoint_index`, `resolve_endpoint`, `endpoint_writes`, `check_request`), `invoke`, `to_plain`, `raise_user_error`, the dropdown loader |
| `_source.py` | `DodoPaymentsWebhookSource(WebhookSource)` (path `dodo-payments`, `StandardWebhooksVerifier`), `shape_dodo_payments_event`, the `get_webhook_source()` singleton |
| `_events.py` | The one CloudEvents type, its factory and the `emit` wrapper |
| `_credentials.py` | `DodoPaymentsCredential` (SDK-free): `_probe` finds the mode, `validate` saves it; `stored_mode` |
| `icon.svg` / `dodo_payments.svg` / `meta.json` | Dodo's brandmark from its media kit (https://dodopayments.com/brand), node and credential icon; colour `#C6FE1E` |

Config touched outside the folder: `config/credential_providers.json` (the
`dodo_payments` card, `kind: "apiKey"`, fields `apiKey` and
`dodo_payments_webhook_key`), `config/employee_apps.json` (the hire app,
`side_effects: "money"`), `config/node_allowlist.json` (`dodoPaymentsAction`),
`nodes/visuals.json` (skill binding), `constants.py` (`dodoPaymentsReceive` in
`EVENT_TRIGGER_TYPES` and `WORKFLOW_TRIGGER_TYPES`), `pyproject.toml` /
`uv.lock`. Paired skill:
[`server/skills/payments_agent/dodo-payments-skill/SKILL.md`](../server/skills/payments_agent/dodo-payments-skill/SKILL.md).

## Clients and retries

`open_client` builds an `AsyncDodoPayments` per operation and closes it after.
Calls that only read keep the SDK's default retries (`READ_RETRIES`, 2, on
connection errors, 408, 409, 429 and 5xx). **Calls that write run with retries
off**: the SDK retries POSTs as well, and Dodo's API takes no idempotency key,
so a retried refund could be refunded twice. A write that times out or meets a
5xx answers that its outcome is unknown and should be looked up before trying
again. Every SDK error becomes a `NodeUserError`, which Temporal never retries,
so an activity retry cannot repeat a write either. The per-request timeout is
60 s (`CALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`); validation uses the credential's probe timeout
and no retries.

## Operations

| Op | SDK call | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `list_payments` | `payments.list` | `customer_id`, `subscription_id`, `product_id`, `payment_status` |
| `get_payment` | `payments.retrieve(payment_id)` | |
| `list_subscriptions` / `get_subscription` | `subscriptions.list` / `.retrieve` | `customer_id`, `product_id`, `subscription_status` |
| `list_customers` / `get_customer` | `customers.list(email)` / `.retrieve` | |
| `list_products` / `get_product` | `products.list` / `.retrieve(id)` | |
| `list_refunds` | `refunds.list` | `customer_id`, `subscription_id`, `refund_status` |
| `list_disputes` | `disputes.list` | `customer_id` |
| `create_checkout_session` | `checkout_sessions.create` | One `product_cart` item; `customer` is `{customer_id}` or `{email, name}`; `discount_codes`; returns `checkout_url` (single use, 24 hours) |
| `create_customer` | `customers.create(email, name)` | Both required by Dodo |
| `create_customer_portal_link` | `customers.customer_portal.create` | `send_email=False`: the link comes back, Dodo emails no one |
| `create_refund` | `refunds.create` | Whole payment; with `product_id` one item (`items=[{item_id}]`); with `amount` too, part of it |
| `cancel_subscription` | `subscriptions.update` | `status="cancelled"`, or `cancel_at_next_billing_date=True` (the SDK has no cancel method) |
| `change_subscription_plan` | `subscriptions.change_plan` | `product_id`, `quantity`, `proration_billing_mode` |
| `call` | `<endpoint>(**request)` | Any indexed method; checked against its parameters before any credential or network use |
| `list_operations` | the endpoint index | No credentials, no network |

**Paging.** Lists answer with one page (`page` from 0, `page_size` up to 100)
and report `count`, `page` and `page_size`. The SDK's own auto-pagination is
not used: after page 0 it asks for page 2 (`next_page_info` assumes a 1-based
start), and Dodo's envelope carries no total.

**Dropdown values.** The status and proration dropdowns copy the SDK's
`Literal`s; a test compares them with `dodopayments.types` so an SDK upgrade
that adds a value fails loudly.

## The endpoint index (`call` and `list_operations`)

Nothing is vendored. `endpoint_index()` reflects a throwaway sync client once
per process: each `functools.cached_property` that builds an API resource,
recursively, and each public method's HTTP verb and path from its generated
source (`self._get(path_template("/x/{id}", ...`, `_get_api_list`, `_post`,
`_patch`, `_put`, `_delete`). Parameters come from the signature, minus the
SDK's per-call keywords (`extra_headers`, `extra_query`, `extra_body`,
`timeout`), which `call` refuses, since `extra_headers` could replace the
Authorization header. Two kinds are left out: local helpers that make no
request (`webhooks.unwrap`), and the whole `webhooks` resource, because
webhook endpoints and their signing secrets configure this integration and a
secret has no use in an agent's hands. A test fails if any other method's
route is missed. Endpoints that answer with a file (invoice PDFs, payout CSVs)
are refused with a clear message.

## Approvals

`ApprovalSpec(operations={"create_refund", "cancel_subscription",
"change_subscription_plan", "call"})` with a `when` test: `call` waits only
when its endpoint is not a GET (an unknown endpoint counts as writing).
While the owner asks first, such a call is held as a draft card ("Make a
change in Dodo Payments", details: operation, payment, subscription, product,
amount, reason, endpoint) and runs after Send and the Undo window. Reads,
checkout links, new customers and portal links run without asking: creating a
link moves no money, and an approved call's result does not reach the
employee, so holding a link would lose it. Unlike Stripe, nothing sets
`refuse_while_asking`, so the owner gets a card instead of a refusal.

## Webhooks

Dodo signs every delivery per Standard Webhooks (`webhook-id`,
`webhook-timestamp`, `webhook-signature`, HMAC-SHA256 under the endpoint's
`whsec_` secret). `StandardWebhooksVerifier` checks the signature and refuses a
timestamp more than five minutes from now (the spec's replay window); the base
`WebhookSource` answers 503 with `Retry-After` when no secret resolves (the
API key must be stored too, since the secret is read through the credential)
and 400 on a bad signature or body. Dodo retries a refused delivery up to 8
times over about a day.

Every event travels under one CloudEvents type,
`com.opencompany.dodo_payments.event.received`, with Dodo's type in `subject`
and `data.event_type`: a deployed listener matches exactly one type. The
envelope id is the `webhook-id`, which stays the same across Dodo's retries,
so a deployed listener drops a retry as a duplicate; `workflow_id` stays unset,
so every deployment carrying the trigger receives it. `handle` hands the event
to the in-process waiter (canvas Run, Temporal-off deploy) and to
`dispatch.emit` with `broadcast=False`: the payload carries customer details
and no client reads it.

Trigger output (`shape_dodo_payments_event`): `event_id`, `event_type`,
`business_id`, `timestamp` (Dodo's ISO string), `payload_type` (`Payment`,
`Subscription`, `Refund`, `Dispute`, ...) and `data`.

## Tests

[`server/tests/nodes/test_dodo_payments.py`](../server/tests/nodes/test_dodo_payments.py)
runs the real SDK with respx at the HTTP transport, so requests are built
exactly as the SDK builds them: registration and flat tool schema, dropdown
values and modes against the SDK, mode detection and the saved mode,
missing-credential envelopes, each typed operation's request, reads retried
and writes not, Dodo's code and message in errors, `call` checks before any
network use, the webhook exclusion, file answers refused, `list_operations`
without credentials, the route pattern covering every SDK method, the approval
rule and card, a clean-interpreter check that importing the plugin never loads
the SDK, the catalogue / skill / app wiring, and for the trigger: signed,
tampered, replayed and secret-less deliveries, the filter on both callers, a
real canvas Run through the event waiter, and the deployed path. The verifier's
window is covered in `tests/services/test_events.py`. `dodo_payments` is in
`_MIGRATED_PLUGINS` of `tests/test_plugin_self_containment.py`, and the tool
name is pinned in `tests/fixtures/tool_names_snapshot.json`.

## Known limits

- One Dodo business per install; a second key replaces the first.
- Invoice PDFs and payout CSVs cannot be fetched through `call`.
- No hire uses `dodoPaymentsReceive` as a trigger yet; `employee_apps.json`
  keeps Dodo a tool-only app, as for Stripe.
- `WebhookSource.receive()` queues each event on a push queue nothing drains
  (shared with Stripe's source).
