| `website/assets/mobile-game.png` | A noodlet game in portrait: black screen, Done and a glass Controls/Keyboard capsule, on-screen d-pad and round buttons | |
| `.github/readme/mobile.png` | The four above side by side | |
| `.github/readme/hero.png` | The same chat list beside the Mac app | Used for the Mac comparison |

No screenshot shows the mobile conversation screen; everything about it below comes from code and the changelog.

## 3. Findings

### 3.1 Platform, shell and navigation

**Platform.** iOS 26.0 minimum, Swift 6, destinations `.iOS` (iPhone and iPad), one app target plus a notification service extension sharing an app group (`Mobile/Project.swift:15`, `:40`, `:73-97`). `ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_GLOBAL_ACCENT_COLOR_NAME` is empty, so the accent is system blue (`Project.swift:69`; changelog 0.5.0 "Apple's system blue"). Background audio mode is on so calls survive a locked screen (`Project.swift:53-54`). URL scheme `noodle` for `noodle://join-hub` invitations (`Project.swift:49`). Permission strings: camera "Noodle takes photos you send or use as your picture, scans the QR code of a Noodle Hub invitation, and noodlets you open use the camera when they ask."; local network "Noodle connects to your Noodle Hub on this network."; microphone "Record voice messages you choose to send, transcribed on this device, talk with bots on calls you start, and let noodlets you open listen when they ask." (`Project.swift:50-52`).

**Root.** With no Hub joined the window shows `JoinView`; otherwise `AgentsView` for all joined Hubs (`App.swift:21-27`). An invitation link opened from outside the app asks first: alert "Join this Hub?", message "Hub key <fingerprint>", buttons "Cancel" / "Join" (`App.swift:30-37`); scanning or pasting inside the app joins straight away (changelog 0.4.0). The system pull-to-refresh spinner is made invisible app-wide (`UIRefreshControl.appearance().tintColor = .clear`, `App.swift:16`) because a custom wordmark replaces it.

**No iPad layout.** There is no `NavigationSplitView`, no `horizontalSizeClass` check and no `userInterfaceIdiom` branch anywhere in the app; the only iPad awareness is copy ("Show on iPad", "Run on iPad" via `UIDevice.current.model`, `ExternalScreen.swift:80-81`, `HubTools.swift:693`) and `verticalSizeClass == .compact` to go full screen in landscape for live views (`HubTools.swift:663-666`, `Noodlets.swift:118`, `:138`). On iPad the list fills the screen and a conversation is pushed over it, with bubbles limited only by a 48 pt opposite-side spacer.

**Navigation model.** One `NavigationStack` with a typed path of `ChatLink { hub: String, thread: UUID }` (`Chats.swift:904`, `:962`, `:1019-1023`, `:1251-1255`). Everything else is a modal: sheets (each with its own `NavigationStack` so sub-pages push inside them), fixed-height bottom sheets, and full-screen covers. A sheet chosen from another sheet opens only after the first is dismissed (`chosen` held, opened in `onDismiss`: `Chats.swift:917-918`, `:1039-1044`, `:1234-1243`; same pattern for pairing, `HubScreens.swift:80-81`, `:115-123`), so two sheets never animate at once.

#### Screen inventory

| Screen | Presentation | Reached from | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Join (wordmark + Pair) | Root | No Hub joined | `HubScreens.swift:11-67` |
| Pairing sources | Bottom sheet, 244 pt (184 without camera) | Pair, Add Hub | `HubScreens.swift:425-475` |
| QR scanner | Sheet, full bleed | Scan QR Code | `HubScreens.swift:1017-1048` |
| Help Me Connect | Sheet | Join failure | `HubScreens.swift:235-351` |
| Chat list | Root of stack | Joined | `Chats.swift:899-1244` |
| More | Bottom sheet, 292 pt | `•••` | `Chats.swift:1259-1282` |
| Conversation | Push | Row or circle tap, notification | `Chats.swift:1431-1892` |
| Bot editor (new or edit) | Sheet | More > New Bot; chat title; row menu | `Chats.swift:2077-2354` |
| Group editor | Sheet | More > New Group; title; menu | `Chats.swift:2387-2543` |
| Shared-bot background | Sheet | Title or menu on a bot shared with you | `Chats.swift:2371-2384` |
| Bot Picture | Push in editor | Avatar "Edit" | `Appearance.swift:203-308` |
| Voice | Push in editor | Voice row | `Calls.swift:487-563` |
| Tools / Computers / Browsers | Push in editor | Rows | `HubTools.swift:208-296` |
| New Tool, Custom MCP Server | Sheet, then push | `+` in Tools | `HubTools.swift:478-638` |
| New Computer / New Browser | Sheet | `+` in Computers/Browsers | `HubTools.swift:400-475` |
| Sharing | Push in editor | Sharing row | `HubTools.swift:300-380` |
| Background | Push in editor | Background row | `Appearance.swift:97-200` |
| Hubs | Sheet | More > Hubs | `HubScreens.swift:517-584` |
| Hub details (profile) | Push in Hubs | Row or info button | `HubScreens.swift:587-684` |
| Your Picture | Sheet | Avatar in Hub details | `Appearance.swift:341-488` |
| Archived | Sheet | Hub details | `HubScreens.swift:687-724` |
| Users, user | Push | Hub details (admins) | `HubScreens.swift:727-903` |
| Pair a Device / Invite | Sheet | Hub details, user | `HubScreens.swift:939-1004` |
| Settings | Sheet | More > Settings | `HubScreens.swift:1051-1102` |
| Message lift overlay | Full-screen cover, clear, self-animated | Long press on a bubble | `MessageActions.swift:87-219` |
| Shared | Sheet | `…` in conversation | `ChatContent.swift:793-845` |
| Live surface / noodlet | Full-screen cover | Live card, Shared | `HubTools.swift:641-779`, `Noodlets.swift:15-288` |
| Web preview | Sheet (`SFSafariViewController`) | Link tap | `ChatContent.swift:346-352` |
| Table | Sheet, medium/large | Table card | `MessageTables.swift:42-72` |
| Transcript (voice), Call transcript | Sheet, medium/large | Long press voice; tap call block | `VoiceMessages.swift:641-654`, `Calls.swift:460-473` |

### 3.2 Joining a Hub

**Join screen.** The Noodle wordmark is stroked full screen at a word width of 220 pt in `.primary` with round caps and joins; once per launch it is "written" with `.easeInOut(duration: 3.4).delay(0.55)`, then the bottom controls fade and rise 12 pt with `.easeOut(duration: 0.5).delay(4.05)`; Reduce Motion shows both at once (`HubScreens.swift:24-31`, `:49-51`, `:54-65`). The only control is a full-width "Pair" (`.borderedProminent`, `.large`) in a 24 pt padded `VStack(spacing: 16)` at the bottom (`HubScreens.swift:32-49`).

**Pairing sources** (bottom sheet, drag indicator, `VStack(spacing: 12)`, padding 24, `.large` controls): "Scan QR Code" (`qrcode.viewfinder`, prominent, only where the camera scanner is supported), the system paste control at 50 pt high (`UIPasteControl`, icon and label, capsule, tint foreground on a 15 % tint background), "Choose Photo" (`photo`, bordered). Heights 244 / 184 pt (`HubScreens.swift:425-475`, `:479-514`). The paste control exists because a paste the person starts is always allowed while reading the clipboard from code is refused.

**While joining** the button area becomes a 50 pt capsule on `.fill.tertiary` with a spinner and "Connecting to <Hub>…" (scales down to 0.7), "Still trying…" fades in above it after 4 s, and "Cancel" sits below (`HubScreens.swift:143-169`). In the Hubs list the same state is a row: spinner, Hub name, "Connecting…" or "Still trying…", borderless Cancel (`HubScreens.swift:172-195`). Failure shows a red `exclamationmark.triangle` label, or, when no address answered, the message in secondary and a bordered "Help Me Connect" (`HubScreens.swift:198-232`).

**Help Me Connect** probes each address kind in order and lists them under "Your Hub": "Home Wi-Fi", "Tailscale", "Internet", each answered by green `checkmark.circle.fill` "Answers" or secondary `xmark.circle` "No answer" (small spinner while checking). Then advice rows with their symbols: "You're offline. Connect to Wi-Fi or mobile data." (`wifi.slash`); "Noodle isn't allowed to look for your Hub on this network. Turn on Local Network for Noodle in Settings." (`lock`, with an "Open Settings" button); "Make sure you're on the same Wi-Fi as the Mac your Hub runs on." or "You're on mobile data. Join the same Wi-Fi as the Mac your Hub runs on." (`wifi`); "Away from that Wi-Fi? Open Tailscale and connect." (`point.3.connected.trianglepath.dotted`); "Your Hub answers now. Tap Try Again." (`checkmark.circle`); "Make sure the Mac your Hub runs on is awake and its Hub is open." (`desktopcomputer`). A prominent full-width "Try Again" is pinned in the bottom safe-area inset with 24 pt padding; "Done" top left (`HubScreens.swift:244-350`).

### 3.3 Chat list (`AgentsView`)

Anatomy on a 390 pt wide phone (values in points; sketch, not to scale):

```text
+----------------------------------------------------------+
| status bar                                               |
|                 All v                         ...        |  inline bar; title = space menu; plain tinted ellipsis
|                                                          |
|    [note]          [note]                                |  note bubble 14 above the circle top
|     (76)            (76)            (76)                 |  pinned circles: 3 columns, gap 12, row gap 16
|     Name            Name            Name                 |  .caption, 1 line
|                                                          |  no separator under the circles or above row 1
| o  (48)  Name     Hub name       2 hr ago             >  |  unread dot 10 at x = 8; row leading inset 26
|          preview, .subheadline secondary, 2 lines        |  HStack spacing 12, vertical padding 4
|         -------------------------------------------------|  separator from the text column; none above row 1
|    (48)  Name                    1 day ago            >  |
|          ...                                             |
|                 [ Search ]                               |  iOS 26: floating glass field (inferred placement)
+----------------------------------------------------------+
```

**Toolbar.** Inline title mode with no title string. The principal slot is the space menu: `Text(spaceTitle).font(.headline)` plus `chevron.down` at `.caption.weight(.semibold)` in secondary, `HStack(spacing: 4)` (`Chats.swift:1092-1120`). The trailing item is a plain tinted `ellipsis` ("More") with the iOS 26 shared glass background hidden, "as in Messages, not the round glass default" (`Chats.swift:1028-1034`). The screenshot shows the blue `•••` and no title.

**Spaces menu**: a picker with "All", then one entry per joined Hub (by Hub name), then a second picker of spaces the person made, a divider, "New Space…" (`plus`), and for a custom space "Rename Space…" (`pencil`) and destructive "Delete Space" (`trash`). Naming uses an alert "New Space" / "Rename Space" with a "Name" field and "Cancel" / "Create" or "Rename" (disabled while blank); deleting asks "Delete <name>?" with "Its bots and groups stay in All." (`Chats.swift:1054-1068`). A space chosen elsewhere that no longer exists falls back to All (`Chats.swift:1122-1125`). Custom spaces sync through iCloud (`Chats.swift:910-912`, `:1073-1079`). A bot or group created while a custom space is shown joins it (`Chats.swift:1157-1161`).

**More sheet**: four full-width `.bordered` `.large` buttons in `VStack(spacing: 12)`, padding 24, fixed detent 292 pt, drag indicator: "New Bot" (`person.badge.plus`), "New Group" (`person.2`), "Hubs" (`server.rack`), "Settings" (`gear`) (`Chats.swift:1259-1282`).

**Pinned circles** (Messages-style): a `LazyVGrid` of 3 flexible columns, column spacing 12, row spacing 16, vertical padding 8 plus 8 more at the top when any of the first three carries a note, no separator (`Chats.swift:969-985`). Each circle is `VStack(spacing: 6)` of a 76 pt `ThreadAvatar` and the name in `.caption`, one line (`Chats.swift:1329-1353`). An unread mark is a 14 pt tint dot at the avatar's top-leading corner with a 2 pt `systemBackground` ring (`Chats.swift:1341-1347`). A note bubble hangs 14 pt above the avatar top: `.caption2` (semibold when it is an unread reply), padding 8 × 4, max width 104, one line, `.regularMaterial` capsule, shadow black 12 % radius 3 y 1 (`Chats.swift:1355-1375`). The note is the start of the latest unread bot reply (whitespace collapsed, tables removed) or else the status the bot set (`Chats.swift:507-514`). Tapping a circle opens the chat; touch and hold opens its menu (a `Menu` with `primaryAction`, because context menus on several cells of one list row all lifted the row and showed the first circle's menu, `Chats.swift:972-978`; changelog 0.13.0 fix).

**Row anatomy** (`AgentRow`, `Chats.swift:1284-1322`; screenshot confirms):

| Element | Value |
|---|---|
| Layout | `HStack(spacing: 12)`, vertical padding 4 |
| Avatar | `ThreadAvatar` 48 pt with phase dot `max(8, 0.24 × size)` = 11.5 pt, 2 pt `systemBackground` ring, bottom-trailing |
| Unread dot | 10 pt tint circle in the left margin, 8 pt from the avatar; the row's leading inset is `2 × 8 + 10 = 26` so the dot is 8 pt from the screen edge too (`Chats.swift:995`, `:1291`, `:1297-1301`) |
| Line 1 | Name `.headline`, 1 line; Hub name `.caption` secondary when several Hubs are shown together; spacer; time `.subheadline` secondary, first-baseline aligned |
| Time format | `.relative(presentation: .numeric, unitsStyle: .abbreviated)`: "2 hr ago", "1 day ago", "3 days ago" |
| Line 2 | Last message preview (tables removed) or the bot's description when there are no messages; `.subheadline` secondary, 2 lines; `VStack(spacing: 2)` |
| Accessory | Disclosure chevron (it is a `NavigationLink`) |
| Separators | Hidden above the first row, visible between rows; start at the text column |

The preview is not stripped of Markdown: the screenshot shows "The \*\*8\*\* carries the goo…" in raw form, because `previewText` only removes tables (`Shared/HubLink/Sources/HubLink/MessageTable.swift:54-59`).

**Ordering.** Pinned first, then newest conversation first, where recency is the latest message's time or the bot's creation time (`Chats.swift:304-318`, `:348-351`). In All, pins belong to this phone (`pins.json`) and pinned items are ordered by recency; in a Hub's space the pins are the Hub's (`pinnedAt`, synced to all devices) and keep the order they were pinned in; in a custom space pins come first in pin order (`Chats.swift:329-341`, `:353-378`, `:1171-1188`). Bots and groups share one list with no section headers. Archived ones leave the list (`Chats.swift:269-279`).

**Search.** `.searchable(prompt: "Search")` (`Chats.swift:1004`). A non-blank query hides the circles and shows one plain list of matches on name, description or any message body held on the phone, ignoring case and accents (`localizedStandardContains`, `Chats.swift:320-327`, `:963-967`). No results shows the system search empty state. On iOS 26 the field is a floating glass capsule at the bottom of the screen (visible in the New Tool screenshot; the chat-list screenshot does not show it, so its exact resting state there is inferred).

**Swipe and touch-and-hold.** Leading swipe on an unpinned row: "Pin" (`pin.fill`) tinted orange; there is no trailing swipe and no delete from the list (`Chats.swift:996-999`). The touch-and-hold menu (same for rows and circles, `Chats.swift:1190-1216`): "Pin" (`pin.fill`) or "Unpin" (`pin.slash.fill`); submenu "Spaces" (`square.stack`) with a toggle per space, divider, "New Space…" (which creates the space with this conversation in it and shows it); then for your own bot or group "Edit Bot…"/"Edit Group…" (`pencil`) and "Archive Bot"/"Archive Group" (`archivebox`), or for a bot someone shared with you only "Change Background…" (`photo`).

**Empty and loading states** (overlay): spinner while any Hub is loading; "Not Connected" (`wifi.exclamationmark`) with the error; "No Bots" (`bubble.left.and.bubble.right`) (`Chats.swift:1005-1017`).

**Pull to refresh** writes the Noodle wordmark (word width 96 pt, stroked in `.primary`) progressively as the list is pulled; it is whole at 80 pt of pull and stays whole in the gap the refresh holds open until the reload finishes (`WordmarkRefresh.swift:14-83`). Used on the chat list, Hubs, Hub details, Users and Tools screens.

**Data rules visible in the UI.** The last sync is cached and shown at launch before the Hub answers (`Chats.swift:96-126`). Each Hub is followed over a live event stream and reconnected 5 s after a failure (`Chats.swift:536-547`); following stops while the app is in the background so the Hub knows to push instead (`Chats.swift:1081-1088`). Unread means a bot message newer than when the conversation was last read on this phone or reported read by another device; the first sync after installing counts everything as read (`Chats.swift:68-70`, `:228-260`, `:616-620`). Opening a conversation marks it read on the Hub and removes its delivered notifications (`Chats.swift:236-247`).

### 3.4 Conversation (`ChatView`)

Anatomy (from code; no screenshot of this screen exists):

```text
+----------------------------------------------------------+
|  <     (28) Name                         phone    ...    |  nav bar over the wallpaper; title opens the editor
|  [ phone.fill 00:42              speaker  mic  end ]     |  call bar, glass capsule, only during a call
|                                                          |
|   wallpaper: full bleed under bars and composer,         |
|   black 25 % scrim unless default                        |
|                                                          |
|   +-------------------------------+                      |  bot: secondarySystemBackground, radius 18,
|   | reply text (17 pt body)       |       >= 48 free     |  padding 12 x 8; leading
|   +-------------------------------+                      |
|                  [react badges]                          |  badges hang 16 above a bubble's top-right corner
|                     +---------------------------------+  |  you: accent fill, white text; trailing
|        >= 48 free   | your message                    |  |
|                     +---------------------------------+  |
|                                          Delivered       |  .caption2, latest own message only
|                                                          |
|  (+)  ( Message ................................ mic )   |  48 high, plus 48 circle, gap 8, side padding 12
+----------------------------------------------------------+  bottom gap max(8, safe-area-bottom - 6); 8 above keyboard
```

Content is padded 12 at the sides, rows 6 apart; in groups a 28 pt avatar column sits left of bot bubbles.

#### 3.4.1 Header and bars

Inline navigation bar. The principal item is a button holding a 28 pt `ThreadAvatar` (with phase dot, 8 pt) and the name in `.headline` `.primary`, `HStack(spacing: 8)`; tapping opens the editor (or only the background editor for a bot shared with you) (`Chats.swift:1567-1576`). Trailing items: `phone` ("Call <name>") when the bot can be called and is not already on a call (`LinkBot.canCall`, Codex bots per changelog 0.21.0), and `ellipsis` ("Shared") when anything live was shared in the conversation (`Chats.swift:1577-1594`). During a call the `CallBar` sits in the top safe-area inset under the navigation bar and the conversation stays usable (`Chats.swift:1557-1560`). A conversation deleted on another device pops itself (`Chats.swift:1481-1482`).

#### 3.4.2 Transcript layout and scrolling

`ScrollView` with a `LazyVStack(spacing: 6)`, horizontal padding 12, vertical 8 (`Chats.swift:1495-1521`, `:1932`). The wallpaper (`ConversationBackdrop`) is the scroll view's background and ignores safe areas, so it runs under the bars and the composer; there is no bar behind the composer (`Chats.swift:1524`, `:1681`). The keyboard dismisses interactively on scroll (`Chats.swift:1523`). No timestamps or date separators appear anywhere in the transcript.

Paging: the first open loads the newest 50 messages; a spinner row at the top loads the previous 50 when it appears; newer messages arrive 100 at a time (`Chats.swift:93-94`, `:828-867`, `:1497-1501`). Rows keep their place by message ID so loading earlier pages does not move what is being read (`Chats.swift:1517-1518`).

Scroll rules (`Chats.swift:1377-1428`, tested in `ConversationScrollTests`): opens at the end; while the end is visible (2 pt tolerance, measured above the composer) it stays at the end as content grows; your own new message always scrolls to the bottom; anyone else's scrolls to show the message's top, and only if you were at the bottom; if you were reading higher up nothing moves. Only the person's own scrolling can move it off the end (rows measured while appearing must not).

#### 3.4.3 Bubbles

| Property | You | Bot | System |
|---|---|---|---|
| Alignment | Trailing, `Spacer(minLength: 48)` before | Leading, `Spacer(minLength: 48)` after | Centred, full width |
| Fill | `.accentColor` (system blue), opaque | `secondarySystemBackground`, opaque | None |
| Text | White; links underlined in white | `.primary`; links tint | `.footnote` secondary, vertical padding 4 |
| Shape | `RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 18, style: .continuous)`, padding 12 × 8 | same | |
| Extras | Delivery line below; red failure mark to the left | In groups: author name above the first of a run, avatar beside the last | |

Sources: `Chats.swift:1938-1980`, `MessageActions.swift:42-83`. The text font is the default `.body` (17 pt at default Dynamic Type, inferred from no explicit font). Text is inline Markdown only (`inlineOnlyPreservingWhitespace`), and only `http`, `https` and `mailto` links stay tappable (`MessageActions.swift:68-82`).

**Groups.** Bot rows always reserve a 28 pt avatar column (`HStack(alignment: .bottom, spacing: 6)`); the avatar appears beside the last message of each consecutive run by one bot, and the bot's name (`.caption` secondary, leading padding 12, top padding 4) above the first (`Chats.swift:516-534`, `:1964-1979`). In one-to-one chats bot messages have no avatar at all. On a 390 pt phone the widest bubble is 318 pt (366 content − 48), or 284 pt for a bot in a group.

**Reaction clearance.** Every row adds `16 − 6 = 10` pt of top padding so a reaction badge (hanging 16 pt above the bubble) never moves the conversation when added (`Chats.swift:1961-1963`, `:1979`).

**Long messages** fold when longer than 1,200 characters or 12 lines, to 8 lines with a "Read more" button (`.subheadline.weight(.semibold)`, plain) that expands the whole message in place (`Chats.swift:1894-1909`, `:2040-2041`, `MessageActions.swift:49-58`).

**Tables.** A Markdown table splits the message into separate bubbles: prose, a table card, more prose; reactions mark the first (`Chats.swift:2012-2022`). The card: `tablecells` (`.title3`, tint), header names joined with " · " (`.subheadline.weight(.semibold)`, 1 line), "1 row"/"N rows" (`.footnote`, foreground at 70 %), trailing `chevron.right` (`.footnote.weight(.semibold)`, 50 %); padding 12 × 10, max width 280, same 18 pt bubble shape and colours (`MessageTables.swift:7-39`). Tapping opens a "Table" sheet (medium/large detents) with a horizontally and vertically scrolling grid: cells `.subheadline.monospacedDigit()`, max width 240, padding 10 × 8, selectable; headers `.footnote.weight(.semibold)`, tap to sort ascending, descending, then original (chevron 9 pt bold, always laid out so widths do not jump); header band `primary` at 6 %; corner radius 12; menu "Table Actions" (`ellipsis`) with "Copy as CSV" (`doc.on.doc`) and "Share CSV" (`square.and.arrow.up`) as `Table.csv` (`MessageTables.swift:42-157`; changelog 0.22.0).

**Press feedback.** While pressed a text bubble scales to 0.96 with `.spring(duration: 0.25)`; a 0.35 s long press lifts it (`Chats.swift:2017-2018`, `:2042`). VoiceOver gets named actions "Copy" and "React" (`Chats.swift:2020`, `:2043`).

#### 3.4.4 Reactions in the transcript

One capsule badge per distinct emoji, overlapping by 6 pt (`HStack(spacing: -6)`), hung on the bubble's top-trailing corner for every author (offset x +10, y −16). Each badge: `.footnote` text "emoji" or "emoji N" when more than one reacted, horizontal padding 6, minimum 28 × 28, your own in solid tint with white text, others on `tertiarySystemBackground`, 2 pt `systemBackground` stroke. Tapping a badge toggles your reaction. They mark the first text bubble, or the attachments when there is no text (`Chats.swift:1987-2007`, `:2052-2063`, `:2021`, `:2032`).

#### 3.4.5 Delivery and failed messages

Only your latest message, and any message the Hub does not have yet, shows a status line (`.caption2`, secondary, red when failed): "Sending…", "Not delivered", "Delivered" or "Sent" (`Chats.swift:672-677`, `:1487-1488`, `:1956-1958`). Sending is optimistic: the message appears at once, files upload first, and it is retried with pauses of 0, 2, 5 and 15 s under the same ID (idempotent) only while it is still the newest message (`Chats.swift:656-749`). A failed message gets a red `exclamationmark.circle` (`.title2`) to the left of the bubble; it is a menu whose section header is the failure reason (or "Not delivered") with "Try Again" (`arrow.clockwise`, only while newest), "Edit and Send" (`pencil`, puts the text and files back in the composer, prepending to any draft) and "Delete" (`trash`, destructive) (`MessageActions.swift:11-27`, `Chats.swift:1864-1879`, `:1948-1953`). Unsent messages survive a relaunch (`unsent.json`). A message of files alone is sent with the body "Sent N attachment(s)", a lone recording with "Voice message", and the bubble hides those bodies (`Chats.swift:698-701`, `:2065-2069`).

#### 3.4.6 Attachments

Order inside a message: text bubbles, then the first public web link's preview card, then attachments (`Chats.swift:2009-2034`).

| Kind | Rendering | Values |
|---|---|---|
| Picture | Inline image, opens Quick Look (swipes through the message's other files) | Fits 240 × 320 (compact 144 × 192 when sharing a row), minimum 44 on each side, corner radius 16; the frame is reserved from the Hub-provided pixel size so nothing jumps; placeholder `secondarySystemBackground` with spinner, height = width × 2/3 when the size is unknown; decoded at 720 px (`ChatContent.swift:113-153`, `:196-204`) |
| Other file | Card | 44 × 44 thumbnail or symbol (radius 8), filename `.subheadline.weight(.medium)` 2 lines, byte size `.caption` secondary, padding 10, max width 260, `secondarySystemBackground` radius 16 (`ChatContent.swift:155-177`); symbols `photo`, `film`, `waveform`, `doc.richtext`, `doc.text`, `doc` (`:222-229`) |
| Live link (browser tab, computer, noodlet) | Card that opens live full screen | 240 × 150 picture radius 12 on `secondarySystemBackground`; a computer without a picture shows its last 14 terminal lines in 7 pt monospaced white 80 % on black; title `.subheadline.weight(.medium)`; whole card padding 8 on `tertiarySystemBackground` radius 16; noodlet menu "Open on iPhone" (or "Open on iPad", `iphone`) / "Open on Hub" (`play.display`) (`ChatContent.swift:73-111`) |
| Web page shared as a file | Link preview card | as below |
| Voice message | Player | see 3.10 Voice messages |

Picture context menu: share, and "Use as Background" (`photo.on.rectangle`) (`ChatContent.swift:61-69`). Layout of several files follows Settings > Attachments: Vertical (default, 4 pt gap), Wrap (side by side, 8 pt), Stack (overlapping, 12 pt row gap, each next file offset by `min(72, 0.42 × width)` and dropped 12 pt, black 30 % shadow radius 3 y 2); in Stack only files that swipe together overlap and live cards and voice messages sit whole above them (`ChatContent.swift:233-326`).

**Link preview card**: 280 wide; image area 280 × 158 on black 28 % (spinner while loading, `link` symbol at 26 pt light when there is no image); title `.subheadline.weight(.semibold)` 2 lines and site `.caption` secondary, padding 12 × 10; `tertiarySystemBackground`, radius 16 (`ChatContent.swift:497-535`). Only public `http(s)` hosts get one (no `.local`, private or link-local IPv4), fetched on the phone with a 10 s timeout, image capped at 560 px JPEG 0.8, cached per conversation for 7 days; a page with no metadata gets a card naming its site (`ChatContent.swift:355-494`). Tapping any web link opens an in-app Safari sheet unless "Preview Web Links" is off (`ChatContent.swift:329-352`, `Chats.swift:1628-1633`).

#### 3.4.7 Composer

```swift
static let controlHeight: CGFloat = 48                       // field and plus height (Chats.swift:1433)
static func composerGap(homeBar: CGFloat) -> CGFloat { max(8, homeBar - 6) }   // :1437
private var composerLift: CGFloat { keyboardUp ? 8 : Self.composerGap(homeBar: homeBar) - homeBar } // :1664
.safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom) { Color.clear.frame(height: Self.controlHeight + 8 + composerLift) } // :1542
```

- **Height parity.** 48 pt is exactly the height of the iOS 26 search field capsule, pinned by a test that measures the system search field (`ComposerSizeTests.swift:7-25`).
- **Vertical position.** With the keyboard down the composer's bottom sits `max(8, safeAreaBottom − 6)` above the screen edge: 28 pt on a phone with a 34 pt home-indicator inset (partly over the home bar, level with the system search field), 8 pt on a phone without one. With the keyboard up it sits 8 pt above the keyboard (changelog 0.14.0 fix). Keyboard state comes from will-show/will-hide notifications (`Chats.swift:1554-1555`).
- **Overlay, not push.** The transcript reserves room for a one-line composer only (48 + 8 + lift); a longer message grows the composer upward over the conversation, which does not move (`Chats.swift:1540-1553`; changelog 0.9.0).
- **Structure** (`Chats.swift:1666-1816`): horizontal padding 12, top 8; above the controls in a `VStack(spacing: 6)`: the @-mention strip, a transient error line (`.footnote`, red, cleared after 6 s), and pending file chips; then a `GlassEffectContainer` `HStack(alignment: .bottom, spacing: 8)` of the plus and the field.
- **Plus**: `plus` at 18 pt medium, secondary, in a 48 × 48 circle with interactive glass ("Add").
- **Field**: a `UITextView` (so a pasted image attaches as "Image.png"), body font, grows to 6 lines then scrolls (`ChatContent.swift:630-696`); placeholder "Message"; vertical padding 13 inside a capsule of min height 48 (`cornerRadius: 24`, regular glass), leading padding 16, trailing 5. Inside on the right: `mic` (18 pt regular, secondary, 30 × 48 hit area, "Record Voice Message") while there is nothing to send, otherwise `arrow.up.circle.fill` at 30 pt in tint ("Send").
- **Disabled** (archived): the field is disabled and the placeholder becomes the reason: "<Name> is archived", "This group is archived", "Every bot in this group is archived" (`Chats.swift:281-291`).
- **Drafts** are kept per conversation on the phone; a draft of only whitespace is discarded so the field returns at its normal size (`Chats.swift:212-223`, `:1526-1530`).
- **Pending file chip**: 32 × 32 thumbnail or symbol (radius 6), filename `.caption` max 120 wide, `xmark.circle.fill` remove ("Remove <name>"), padding 6, `secondarySystemBackground` capsule; chips scroll horizontally with 6 pt spacing (`ChatContent.swift:538-561`).
- **@-mentions**: typing `@` after whitespace or one of `([{,:` plus up to 64 letters, digits or ` '-_.` shows a horizontal strip of matching non-archived bots (a group's own bots, or all your bots with the current one first, then alphabetical); each chip is a 22 pt avatar and name (`.subheadline`) on a `secondarySystemBackground` capsule, padding 8 × 5, spacing 6; choosing writes the plain name and a trailing space when at the end (`ChatContent.swift:734-774`, `Chats.swift:1818-1846`).

**Attach panel** (Messages-style morph, `Chats.swift:1719-1780`): tapping the plus dismisses the keyboard and, with `.bouncy(duration: 0.4, extraBounce: 0.05)`, morphs the glass circle (shared `glassEffectID("attach")`) into a 230 pt wide glass panel with corner radius 28 and padding 8 that grows up over the conversation from the plus's bottom-left without moving the field. Rows (`VStack(spacing: 2)`): a 32 pt circle with a gradient of the row's colour holding a white 15 pt semibold symbol, then the title in `.body`; spacing 14, horizontal padding 8, min height 48. Rows: "Camera" (`camera.fill`, gray; only with a camera), "Photos" (`photo.on.rectangle.angled`, blue), "Files" (`folder.fill`, cyan). The conversation behind is covered with `.ultraThinMaterial`; tapping it, or the field, closes the panel. Photos allows up to 10 images or videos, named "Photo N.<ext>" or "Video N.<ext>" from the item's own type; the camera saves JPEG 0.9 "Photo.jpg"; Files allows any type, several at once (`Chats.swift:1610-1626`, `ChatContent.swift:563-594`).

#### 3.4.8 Shared sheet

`…` opens "Shared": every computer, browser tab and noodlet shared in the conversation, newest first, one entry per target (a computer whatever its view, a browser per tab); rows with a 96 × 64 picture or symbol (radius 8, `tertiarySystemBackground`), title (2 lines) and kind "Browser", "Computer" or "Noodlet" (`.caption`); "Done" (`ChatContent.swift:792-845`, `HubTools.swift:781-848`). Choosing closes the sheet and opens the item full screen once the sheet is gone (`Chats.swift:1596-1608`).

### 3.7 New bot, groups and the bot editor

**Bot editor** (`AgentEditor`, `Chats.swift:2076-2354`; screenshot `mobile-new-bot.png`). A sheet with its own stack, a grouped `Form`, no navigation title, toolbar "Cancel" and "Create" (new) or "Save" (edit), rendered as glass capsules in the screenshot; while saving the confirm button becomes a spinner. A new bot starts with an empty name, the `sparkles` symbol and a random colour index (`Chats.swift:2100-2101`). Sections in order:

1. Avatar 88 pt with "Edit" (`.subheadline`, tint) below, on a clear row, pushing "Bot Picture" (`Chats.swift:2161-2174`).
2. "Name" text field.
3. "Hub" picker (new bot with several Hubs only); "Harness" menu picker whose items show the provider name with the profile as a subtitle and whose chosen value reads "Provider · Profile" on one line, middle-truncated, or "Choose"; "Model" ("Default" or "Choose" when the plan restricts models); "Effort" ("Default" plus the model's efforts) only when the model offers them; "Voice" (value "Automatic" until chosen) only when the harness has voices. With no harness lent: "Your plan lends no harnesses" (`Chats.swift:2178-2229`, `:2545-2550`). Changing harness clears the effort, sets the harness's initial model and drops a voice the new harness does not offer (`Chats.swift:2124-2134`). An agent's current harness, model or effort that the plan no longer lends is kept at the top of its list so it still displays (`Chats.swift:2104-2156`).

Create/Save is disabled until there is a name and a harness, and a model when the plan restricts models (`Chats.swift:2293-2295`). ### 3.10 Voice messages

**Recording** replaces the field in the composer slot: a regular-glass rounded rectangle (radius 18), padding 12 × 4, with a matching hit shape so taps beside controls do not reach the conversation (`Chats.swift:1668-1675`). Contents (`VoiceMessages.swift:387-458`), `HStack(spacing: 10)`: `xmark` discard (30 × 36); while preparing or finishing a spinner and `.caption` secondary text ("Preparing speech…", "Downloading speech model…", "Starting microphone…", "Finishing transcription…"); while recording a 6 pt red dot and a live waveform 22 pt high; the time `m:ss` in `.caption.monospacedDigit()`; `stop.fill` (30 × 36); and a 30 pt `arrow.up.circle.fill` send that is enabled while recording or ready (sending while recording stops first). Errors show in red `.caption`; after a failed transcription with audio kept, "Retry Transcription" and "Send Audio Only". The limit is 10 minutes (600 s). Transcription runs on device as the person speaks; a partial or failed transcript is never sent without asking (`VoiceMessages.swift:9-264`).

**Live waveform**: bars 2.5 wide every 5 pt, scrolling right to left at a fixed 50 ms per bar a quarter second behind the clock, 12 s kept, height mapped from a fixed −60 to −12 dB range, minimum 2, corner 1.25, `.primary` at 70 % (`VoiceMessages.swift:460-515`).

**Player** in the transcript: a 250 pt card on `secondarySystemBackground` (radius 16, padding 12 × 7): play/pause (28 × 32), the waveform (28 pt high, up to 60 bars, square-root amplitude, minimum 2, 2 pt gaps, radius 2, played part accent, rest secondary 60 %) that seeks on tap, and the time in `.caption.monospacedDigit()` secondary (duration, or position while playing). Touch and hold offers "Show Transcript" (`text.quote`), a "Transcript" sheet at medium/large ("No transcript available."). One recording plays at a time, through the speaker even in Silent Mode (`VoiceMessages.swift:537-662`). A recording is sent as "Voice message.caf" with the transcript, duration and waveform as metadata.

### 3.11 Calls

`PhoneCalls` allows one call per Hub; starting another hangs up the first (`Calls.swift:28-146`). Audio runs in a hidden 1 × 1 transparent `WKWebView` doing WebRTC; the Hub only relays the offer and answer and receives spoken lines; the call starts on the earpiece at full voice quality and "Speaker" switches to voice-chat processing for echo cancellation; AirPods use A2DP (`Calls.swift:148-308`). The timer and a chime start only when both the Hub and the media say connected.

**Call bar** (`Calls.swift:344-389`): a glass capsule in the top inset with horizontal padding 18, vertical 10, outer padding 16 horizontal and 4 top, `HStack(spacing: 14)`, `.body.weight(.medium)`: `phone.fill` (secondary while connecting, green when connected), the elapsed time in a slot as wide as "00:00" ("--:--" while connecting; "h:mm:ss" past an hour), spacer, Speaker (`speaker.fill` / `speaker.wave.3.fill`, accent when on), Mute (`mic.fill` / `mic.slash.fill`), End (`phone.down.fill`, red).

**In the transcript**: a full-width card "Voice call with <name>" (`.subheadline.weight(.medium)`) with a live timer or the final length (hours, minutes and seconds in abbreviated units; a rendering such as "2 min, 5 sec" is inferred), `phone` or green `phone.fill`, padding 14 × 9, `.ultraThinMaterial` radius 14. Spoken lines appear as transcript blocks placed after the last message sent before they were said, so typing during a call splits the transcript: `waveform` icon, two-line preview (a live block shows its last two lines, a finished one its first two), speaker in `.footnote.weight(.semibold)` secondary ("You" or the bot's name) followed by the line in `.subheadline`, "N lines" in `.caption2` tertiary, padding 14 × 8, `.ultraThinMaterial` radius 12, inset 24 pt from the sides; tapping opens a "Call" sheet listing every line (`Calls.swift:310-342`, `:391-477`).

### 3.12 Live views and noodlets on mobile

**Live surface** (a shared browser tab or computer, or a noodlet streamed from the Hub) opens as a full-screen cover on black (`HubTools.swift:640-779`). In portrait: inline navigation bar with the card's title (or "Live"), "Done", and a primary group of "Show on TV" (`tv`) for games, "Controls" (`gamecontroller.fill` / `gamecontroller`), "Keyboard" (`keyboard`) and "Run on iPhone" (`iphone`) for a noodlet that can run locally. In landscape (compact vertical size) or on TV the bar and status bar hide and the same buttons float icon-only in `.buttonStyle(.glass)` over the top corners, 12 pt from the sides. Touch and hold then move drags; two-finger pinch zooms and pans (changelog 0.11.0). A noodlet with game controls shows an on-screen gamepad; a connected hardware controller hides the buttons it covers.

**Noodlets** (`Noodlets.swift:13-288`): a noodlet runs on the phone in a web view (files fetched once per revision and cached; its data and secrets stay on the Hub) or streams from the Hub; the choice is remembered per noodlet, and the card's menu chooses before opening; noodlets using camera, microphone or screen always run on the phone (changelog 0.12.0). On first use of declared permissions it asks: "“<title>” would like to use <Camera and Microphone>." with "Allow" / "Don’t Allow"; a refusal shows "Permission was not given to use …" (`Applet/Protocol/Sources/NoodletRuntime/Grants.swift:41-52`). A noodlet laid out for desktop gets the desktop site unless it declares itself an app (`Noodlets.swift:143-147`). It can lock orientation and request full screen; sound plays in Silent Mode and mixes with other audio; the idle timer is disabled while a controller is connected or the game is on a TV.

**On-screen gamepad** (`Shared/Surface/Sources/Surface/Gamepad.swift:165-263`, `:350-450`; screenshot `mobile-game.png`): margin 16 inside the safe area, spacing 12; pad size `clamp(0.36 × min(width, height), 120, 170)`, bottom-left; a 64 × 44 menu capsule above it; buttons `clamp(0.42 × pad, 52, 72)` in up to 3 columns nearest the right thumb (two buttons sit on a slant, the main one 45 % of a button higher); at most 8 buttons; eight-way pads with a 25 % dead zone; sticks whose knob travels half the radius. Buttons are circles on black 25 % plus white 20 % (45 % pressed), 1.5 pt white 40 % stroke, labels 13 pt semibold white.

### 3.13 External screen (TV)

On iOS 27 only, the app offers a TV scene accessory (`sceneAccessory` with `ExternalNonInteractiveAccessory`). While Screen Mirroring or a cable gives a TV, a noodlet with game controls plays full screen on the TV (sized for the TV) and the phone turns to landscape and shows only the controls, or, when a hardware controller covers every button, a list of connected controllers (vendor logo `logo.xbox`, `logo.playstation` or `gamecontroller.fill` at `.title` in a 44 pt column, name in `.title3`, battery symbol), white on black, refreshed every 30 s. "Show on iPhone"/"Show on iPad" brings the game back without restarting; "Show on TV" sends it again or, with no TV, alerts "No TV Connected" / "Turn on Screen Mirroring in Control Center, or connect a TV with a cable." Without a game open the TV mirrors the phone (`ExternalScreen.swift:6-155`; changelog 0.17.0 and 0.18.0). A controller's View button shows a TV menu over the game: black 55 % scrim, a horizontal row of 300 × 180 cards (radius 16, white 12 % fill, spacing 28, padding 60 × 40, 40 from the bottom), the chosen card raised 1.08 with a 4 pt white border and the rest at 70 %, titles in `.title3`, a final "Close Game" (`xmark` 48 pt); d-pad moves, A opens, B or View resumes (`ExternalScreen.swift:157-294`).

### 3.14 Appearance: wallpapers and avatars

**`ConversationBackdrop`** (`Appearance.swift:8-59`): a `systemBackground` base; a photo scaled to fill; a video shown as its poster with a muted `AVPlayerLooper` (aspect fill, does not keep the display awake) on top unless Reduce Motion is on; or a preset drawn as a top-leading to bottom-trailing linear gradient of three colours plus an ellipse of the middle colour at 50 %, sized 1.4 × width by 1.1 × height, rotated −35°, offset 0.35 × width, blurred 50. Any non-default background gets a black 25 % scrim. It ignores safe areas and hit testing. The four presets (sRGB 0-1), shared with the Mac:

| Preset | Colour 1 | Colour 2 | Colour 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sunset | 0.96, 0.52, 0.15 | 0.77, 0.43, 0.67 | 0.46, 0.35, 0.75 |
| Ocean | 0.04, 0.26, 0.50 | 0.08, 0.60, 0.66 | 0.14, 0.30, 0.62 |
| Forest | 0.08, 0.24, 0.18 | 0.34, 0.53, 0.30 | 0.14, 0.34, 0.39 |
| Dusk | 0.18, 0.16, 0.39 | 0.47, 0.29, 0.60 | 0.73, 0.37, 0.47 |

The background is kept on the Hub for every device; the phone fetches a small copy and forgets copies no conversation uses (`Chats.swift:133-210`).

**`BackgroundEditor`** ("Background", `Appearance.swift:95-200`): a 200 pt preview (radius 16, edge to edge) of the backdrop with two sample bubbles on `.regularMaterial` capsules, padding 10, `VStack(spacing: 14)`, padding 20: "Make this space your own." (left) and "Looks good!" (right). Then a row of five swatches (spacing 10): "Default", "Sunset", "Ocean", "Forest", "Dusk", each a 44 pt tall rendered backdrop, radius 8, border 2 pt accent when selected or 0.5 pt separator, title `.caption2`. Then "Choose Photo" and "Create Image" (Image Playground shaped like the screen, starting from the current photo). Changes apply immediately on the Hub.

**Avatars.** `AgentAvatar` (`Chats.swift:2598-2653`): a photo, or a symbol at 0.45 × size semibold white on one of six gradients (top-leading to bottom-trailing): blue to cyan, purple to pink, orange to yellow, mint to teal, indigo to blue, pink to orange; any stored colour index wraps modulo 6. Phase dot colours: working blue, failed red, ready green, offline or starting gray. `ThreadAvatar` for groups (`Chats.swift:2552-2596`): one active member is drawn at 0.86 × size offset by (−6 %, −6 %) in front of a `.quaternary` disc of 0.88 × size offset (+6 %, +6 %); several members draw up to three avatars at 0.62 × size at offsets (−18 %, −14 %), (+18 %, −14 %) and (0, +19 %) on a full `.quaternary` disc; every member avatar has a 2 pt `systemBackground` ring; archived bots leave the picture. `PersonAvatar` (`Appearance.swift:310-337`): a photo, a symbol at 0.45 × size, or initials (first letters of the first two words, uppercase) at 0.4 × size semibold rounded, white on the same gradients; with no choice the colour comes from the first byte of the person's ID (`LinkProtocol.swift:665-670`).

**`PersonPictureEditor`** ("Your Picture", `Appearance.swift:339-488`): 104 pt preview; "Photo": "Take Photo" (`camera`, square crop), "Choose Photo", "Create Image", destructive "Remove Photo" (`trash`); "Colour" as for bots; "Symbol": an initials tile then `person.fill`, `face.smiling`, `star.fill`, `heart.fill`, `leaf.fill`, `pawprint.fill`, `music.note`, `gamecontroller.fill`, `book.fill`, `cup.and.saucer.fill`, `sun.max.fill`; "Cancel" / "Done" (Done is a no-op close when nothing changed).

### 3.15 Notifications

Each joined Hub is given a random topic stored in that Hub's folder; the phone subscribes in CloudKit's public database to records the Hub leaves under that topic while replies wait unread, and tells the Hub the topic only once listening works (`Notifications.swift:14-90`, `ReplyNotifications.swift:23-54`). The push carries only the topic and conversation; its default text is "New reply" with the default sound; a collapse ID per conversation makes a newer one replace the older; mutable content lets the notification service extension ask the Hub directly for the bot's name (title) and its latest reply (body, tables removed; a reply of files alone shows the first filename or "Attachment"), within the extension's time limit, otherwise it shows "New reply" (`ReplyNotifications.swift:56-80`, `NotificationService.swift:4-37`). Notifications stack per conversation (`threadIdentifier`). The extension looks the conversation up among bots only, so a group's notification stays "New reply" (inferred from `ReplyNotifications.swift:74-77`). Permission is asked only once a Hub exists (alert, sound, badge). In the foreground no banner is shown (`willPresent` returns no options, `Notifications.swift:158-163`). Tapping opens the conversation once its Hub has loaded (`Chats.swift:1225-1232`). Reading a conversation removes its delivered notifications. **There is no inline reply**: no notification category, action or text-input action exists anywhere in the mobile sources.

### 3.16 Key values at a glance

## 4. Web translation

**Breakpoints** (proposed; Noodle itself has one phone layout for every width):

| Width | Layout |
|---|---|
| < 768 px | Phone: stack navigation. Route `/` is the list, `/c/:hub/:thread` the conversation, pushed with a horizontal slide; back gesture or button pops. Editors as full-height bottom sheets; small choices as content-height sheets; live views and the lift overlay as full-viewport layers |
| 768-1023 px | Two panes when landscape-ish: list 320 px plus conversation; or keep the phone stack in portrait tablets. Do not copy Noodle's iPad behaviour of stretching the phone layout |
| ≥ 1024 px | Sidebar (320-360 px) plus conversation, Mac-style header; dialogs centred instead of bottom sheets |

**Conversation column.** Content padding 12 px; bubble `max-width: min(100% - 48px, 560px)` (Noodle has no cap; add one for tablets and desktop). Row gap 6 px plus 10 px reserved top padding on every row for the 16 px reaction overhang. Bubble radius 18 px, padding 12 × 8 px, 17 px body text on phones (at least 16 px in any `<input>`/`<textarea>` so iOS Safari does not zoom on focus; web platform note).

**Composer and the on-screen keyboard.** Position the composer absolutely at the bottom over the transcript; give the transcript a bottom padding of one composer line only (48 + 8 + lift); let a multi-line field grow upward to 6 lines and then scroll, without changing the transcript's padding. Bottom offset with the keyboard closed: `max(8px, env(safe-area-inset-bottom) - 6px)` (needs `viewport-fit=cover`); with it open: 8 px above the keyboard. On iOS Safari read the keyboard height from `visualViewport` (`innerHeight - visualViewport.height - visualViewport.offsetTop`) on `resize`/`scroll`; on Chromium `navigator.virtualKeyboard.overlaysContent = true` with `env(keyboard-inset-height)` or `interactive-widget=resizes-content` in the viewport meta are alternatives (web platform notes, verify per browser). Keep the composer 48 px tall with a 48 px circular plus on its left, mic or send inside the pill on the right; swap mic for send as soon as there is text or a pending file. Close the keyboard when the attach panel opens (`blur()` the field) and when the transcript is scrolled by touch.

**Scrolling.** Implement Noodle's three rules: stick to the bottom only while the bottom is visible (2 px tolerance measured above the composer); always scroll to your own sent message; for an incoming message scroll to its top only if the person was at the bottom. Use `overflow-anchor` or ID-keyed restoration when prepending earlier pages; reserve image boxes from known pixel sizes (fit 240 × 320, compact 144 × 192, minimum 44) so loads never shift.

**Touch targets and gestures.** Keep 44 px minimums: plus 48, field 48, mic and send 30 × 48 (widen to 44 on web), attach rows ≥ 48, reaction cells 44, menu items ≈ 50. Noodle's 28 px reaction badges, 22 px mention chips and 30 × 36 recording buttons are below 44 px; enlarge hit areas with padding or pseudo-elements. Long press 350 ms opens the lift overlay (press scale 0.96 during the hold; suppress `-webkit-touch-callout` and text selection during the press); provide the same actions on right-click, keyboard (`ContextMenu` key / Shift+F10) and a visible button, and the same Pin action as a swipe on touch and in the context menu (the swipe must never be the only path).

**Component mapping.**

| Noodle construct | Web (React + Tailwind + shadcn/Radix) |
|---|---|
| `NavigationStack` push | Router routes with a slide transition on phones; panes on wide screens |
| `.sheet` with detents (292, 244, medium/large) | shadcn Drawer (Vaul) with snap points, drag handle visible |
| Full-screen cover (lift overlay, live views) | Full-viewport layer with its own enter/exit animation; `inert` on the page behind |
| `Menu` with `primaryAction` on pinned circles | Click navigates; long-press or right-click opens a Radix `DropdownMenu`/`ContextMenu` |
| `.swipeActions(edge: .leading)` | Pointer-event swipe revealing an orange "Pin" action, plus the same item in the context menu |
| `.searchable` | A search `Input` pinned at the top of the list (a bottom field mimicking iOS 26 is optional) |
| Liquid Glass (`glassEffect`) | Translucent fill + `backdrop-filter: blur() saturate()` + hairline highlight; Noodle defines no numbers (system material) |
| `GlassEffectContainer` morph of plus into panel | Shared-layout animation (for example a FLIP or View Transitions) from the 48 px circle to the 230 px radius-28 panel, spring roughly 400 ms with slight overshoot |
| `UIPasteControl` | A "Paste" button calling `navigator.clipboard.readText()` on the user's tap |
| QR scanner | `BarcodeDetector` where available, otherwise a JS decoder over `getUserMedia` |
| `SFSafariViewController` preview | Most sites refuse framing; use the link card and open in a new tab |
| Quick Look gallery | Lightbox swiping through the message's files |
| `AVPlayerLooper` wallpaper | `<video muted loop playsinline autoplay poster>`; `prefers-reduced-motion` shows the poster only |
| On-device transcription | Web Speech API where available, or server transcription; `MediaRecorder` for audio |
| Hidden WebRTC web view | WebRTC directly in the page |
| CloudKit push + service extension | Web Push with a service worker that fetches the reply text from your server on push, keeping message text out of the push payload |

**Safe areas.** `viewport-fit=cover`; nav bar top padding `env(safe-area-inset-top)`; the wallpaper must extend under both bars; landscape game controls and floating Done buttons must respect left/right insets (Noodle keeps the gamepad 16 px inside the safe area).

**Colours.** System blue accent and semantic surfaces map to tokens: accent (iOS system blue, light #007AFF / dark #0A84FF), `secondarySystemBackground` (light #F2F2F7 / dark #1C1C1E), `tertiarySystemBackground` (light #FFFFFF / dark #2C2C2E), `systemBackground` (#FFFFFF / #000000); these hex values are Apple's published system colours (iOS 26 may adjust them slightly), not values from the repository.

**Time.** Format list times as "2 hr ago", "1 day ago", "3 days ago"; `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` with `style: 'short'` produces "2 hr. ago" in en-US, so a small formatter is needed to match.

## 5. Patterns worth copying, and pitfalls to avoid

### Patterns worth copying

- **Composer height equals the search field height** (48), and the composer bottom sits where the list's search field sits, so moving from list to chat feels continuous.
- **Overlay composer growth**: only one line is reserved; long drafts cover the transcript instead of jumping it.
- **Reserved reaction clearance** on every row so reacting never reflows the conversation.
- **Reserved media boxes** from server-provided pixel sizes.
- **Three-rule auto-scroll** (stick only at bottom, own message always, incoming from its top).
- **Optimistic sending with bounded, idempotent retries** (0, 2, 5, 15 s, same ID, only while newest), and a failure mark offering Try Again / Edit and Send / Delete instead of a global error.
- **Per-conversation drafts** that discard whitespace-only text.
- **Pinned circles with a one-line note** (unread reply in semibold, else the bot's status): a strong at-a-glance team view.
- **Sequential modals**: open the next sheet only after the previous one dismissed.
- **Group run grouping**: name above the first message of a run, avatar beside the last, a reserved avatar column so bubbles align.
- **Folding** at 1,200 characters or 12 lines to 8 lines with "Read more".
- **Tables as cards on small screens** that open a sortable, copyable sheet.
- **Messages-style lift overlay** with geometry that keeps the bar and menu on screen and shows the start of very tall messages.
- **Disabled composer that explains itself** through its placeholder.
- **Help Me Connect**: per-route reachability plus plain-language advice and a single Try Again.
- **Notifications that keep content off the push service** and collapse per conversation, cleared when read anywhere.
- **Wordmark pull-to-refresh** as a brand moment that also communicates pull progress.

### Pitfalls to avoid

- **No tablet layout.** iPad shows the stretched phone list and full-width bubbles; build two panes at wider breakpoints.
- **Opaque mobile bubbles vs translucent Mac bubbles** over the same wallpaper: decide one rule per theme rather than diverging silently.
- **Small touch targets** (28 px badges, 22 px mention chips, 30 × 36 recording controls).
- **Markdown leaking into previews** ("The \*\*8\*\* carries…" in the list): strip inline Markdown for list rows, notes and notifications.
- **No timestamps in the transcript** at all; consider timestamps on demand (tap or hover) and day separators.
- **Hierarchical colour surprises**: catalogue names render in tint blue only because of how SwiftUI resolves `.primary` inside list buttons; choose such colours deliberately on the web.
- **Group notifications** probably fall back to "New reply"; and there is no inline reply, which a web build could add where `Notification` actions allow it.
- **Gesture-only actions**: swipe-to-pin and long-press must have visible or keyboard equivalents.
- **In-app web preview** does not translate to the web (frame blocking); do not promise it.

## 6. Open questions and inferences

- The resting state of the iOS 26 bottom search field on the chat list is not visible in `mobile-chats.png`; its bottom placement is inferred from the New Tool screenshot and from the composer-parity test.
- `website/assets/mobile-chats.png` predates 0.23.0 (no "All" title menu), and `mobile-new-bot.png` appears to predate 0.13.0 (no Kick/New Session section above "Delete Bot"); appearance of newer elements is from code only.
- The conversation screen has no screenshot; bubble, composer and overlay appearance are from code and changelog.
- Text size is inferred to be `.body` (17 pt at default Dynamic Type) because `MessageText` sets no font.
- System empty-state copy for search ("No Results for …") and glass material numbers are system-defined and not in the repository.
- Group notifications showing only "New reply" is inferred from the extension looking up bots only.
- Only Codex bots can be called today (changelog 0.21.0); the code gates on the Hub's `canCall`, so other harnesses may follow.
- The external-screen TV mode needs iOS 27; on iOS 26 the TV simply mirrors the phone.

# OpenCompany frontend research snapshot, mapped against Noodle

> Historical research snapshot: the original OpenCompany source revision was not recorded.
> Stop and chat behavior described below predates execution-control commit
> `516ecaca`. For current acknowledged Stop/Resume and chat protocol v2, use
> [workflow control](../../../temporal-workflow-control.md) and
> [chat protocol](../../../chat_protocol.md). The inventory is retained as
> research evidence rather than a maintained runtime contract.

Research note 11 of 11 for the Noodle RFC. The other ten notes analyse Noodle's UI;
this one records what OpenCompany's own frontend already has, where it lives, what
feeds it, and which rules any Noodle-like work must obey. It describes the state
observed during that research review and proposes no design.

## Summary

- **OpenCompany already has a conversation-first owner screen.** Normal mode ("Home",
  `client/src/features/home/`) is a team sidebar of AI employees (round avatar, status
  pip, name, role), a header naming the employee on screen, a shared chat
  (`client/src/features/chat/`) with right-aligned owner bubbles and left-aligned,
  bubble-less replies beside the employee's avatar, a composer with Attach, paste and
  drop, dictation, slash commands, Web and Ask first chips and a round Send/Stop button,
  and a right-hand Workspace dock with Browser, Canvas and Mobile tabs.
- **A Noodle "bot" is closest to an OpenCompany "employee", which is one saved
  workflow.** The employee id is the workflow id, the name is the workflow name, and the
  conversation is the chat session whose id is that workflow id. That coupling is the
  biggest structural difference from Noodle: a chat session belongs to exactly one
  workflow, answers only its owner, follows the workflow's control state (send, queue or
  closed), allows one live answer at a time, and is cleared by a Reset.
- **The chat is richer than Noodle's in agent-specific areas**: AG-UI style streamed
  runs with tool steps, generated UI (json-render, 12 components), approval cards with
  Undo, edit and regenerate branches with version steppers, Good/Bad ratings, numbered
  citations, follow-up suggestions and document cards that open the Canvas.
- **The main gaps against Noodle**: no group conversations (one persona per chat, one
  workflow per session, no @mentions), no sidebar search, sections, previews, timestamps
  or unread markers, no wallpapers or glass surfaces (Home is light and dark only, and blur
  exists only on scrims), no emoji reactions (only thumbs up/down on replies), no voice
  messages or calls (dictation only), no screen capture or annotation, no link unfurls,
  no chat effects, no message context menu, no floating windows, no Hub sharing (multi-user
  mode has no data isolation), no MCP connectors in Home, no keybinding settings, and no
  harness, model or backstory editing from Home.
- **Strict frontend rules apply**: shadcn primitives, `ActionButton` intents, token-only
  Tailwind, no opacity arithmetic, no palette names, lucide icons, Zustand slice
  selectors, TanStack Query for server state, snake_case on the wire, CloudEvents
  broadcasts, the WCAG 2.5.7 drag alternative, and the chat protocol's
  change-the-doc-in-the-same-commit rule.

## Scope (files read)

Documentation:

- `CLAUDE.md` (section 7 "Frontend Design + Theme System (strict)" at `CLAUDE.md:449`,
  section 8 "Naming Conventions" at `CLAUDE.md:469`, "Frontend Performance Architecture"
  at `CLAUDE.md:543`, "Normal/Dev Mode Toggle" at `CLAUDE.md:936`, "Console Panel" at
  `CLAUDE.md:951`, and the broadcast notes at `CLAUDE.md:2791` and `CLAUDE.md:2812`).
- `docs-internal/normal_mode.md`, `docs-internal/chat_protocol.md` (client, messages,
  generated UI, approvals, attachments, branches, feedback, sources, error codes),
  `docs-internal/frontend_architecture.md`, `docs-internal/theme_system.md` (token tiers,
  Home tokens, anti-patterns, class registry), `docs-internal/design-system/IMPLEMENTATION.md`,
  `docs-internal/design-system/HANDOFF.md` (skimmed), `docs-internal/browser_workspace.md`,
  `docs-internal/canvas_node.md` (skimmed), `docs-internal/employee_teams.md`,
  `docs-internal/agent_teams.md` (opening), `docs-internal/browser.md` (profiles section),
  `docs/mobile-workspace.md` (opening).
- The local, gitignored design handoff `design_handoff_opencompany_home/` (its
  `chat/README.md`, `tokens/chat.css`, `tokens/home.css`, a keyword scan of

## Findings

### 1. Shell, screens and the theme rule

- **Two screens, one switch.** `useAppStore.shellMode` (`'normal' | 'dev'`, persisted as
  `ui_shell_mode`) selects Home or the workflow editor; both are lazy chunks
  (`client/src/app/ShellModeSwitch.tsx`). Switching always goes through `enterNormal` /
  `enterDev` (`client/src/app/useShellActions.ts`), never `setShellMode`. The switch is
  `ModeToggle` (`client/src/components/shell/ModeToggle.tsx:19-52`, a segmented
  `ToggleGroup`), shown in the Home header and the editor toolbar, plus Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+D.
  `VITE_NORMAL_MODE=false` turns Home off.
- **App shell.** `client/src/app/AppShell.tsx:86-101` owns the decorative `.app-frame`,
  boot effects (sound sync, page-activity pause, current-workflow sync, saved-graph sync,
  UI defaults, the mode shortcut, orb disposal) and the app-level Settings and
  Credentials dialogs.
- **Home is light and dark only.** `client/src/app/ShellThemeProvider.tsx:14-17` passes
  `baseOnly` to `ThemeProvider` while Home shows, so a stylized theme chosen in Dev shows
  as its family's base (Atomic as light, Cyber as dark) and applies again in Dev. The
  pre-paint script in `client/index.html` applies the same rule to the first frame. The theme
  button (`client/src/features/home/header/ThemeButton.tsx:20-41`) flips light and dark
  with a circular View Transition reveal from the button.

### 4. Home data layer, WebSocket requests and broadcasts

State ownership follows the repo rule: server data in TanStack Query, UI state in a
Zustand store.

- **`useHomeStore`** (`client/src/features/home/state/homeStore.ts:82-219`): `view`
  (`{kind:'hire'} | {kind:'employee', workflowId}`, line 15), sidebar open (persisted
  `home_sidebar_open`), Settings open, tab and category, the new-hire row glow and logo
  pulse nonces, a composer-focus nonce, the hire notice, and the Workspace (open, width
  and tab persisted under `home_workspace_v1`; `workspaceFor`, `workspaceWide` and a
  Canvas focus request kept per session). It holds no server data by design (lines 1-7).
- **Team queries** (`client/src/features/home/data/employees.ts`): `useEmployeesQuery`
  (`list_employees`, `staleTime` 30 s, `refetchOnMount: 'always'`, lines 36-53) and
  `useEmployeeDetailQuery` (`get_employee`; with `live` it polls every 5 s while work is
  active and every 15 s otherwise, and invalidates at most every 3 s on node-status
  changes, lines 55-100). Summaries are parsed forgivingly with zod
  (`client/src/features/home/data/schemas.ts:38-86`).
- **Presentation** (`client/src/features/home/data/presentation.ts`): maps server status
  to pill tone and label (`working`, `ready`, `paused`, `attention`, and `waiting`
  "Needs you" when drafts or a browser request wait, lines 52-105), the main action
  (Pause, Resume, Start, Connect an app, Connect an AI model, Open in Dev mode), and the
  message-box mode (`send`, `queue`, `start`, lines 134-151). Token classes live there
  too (lines 190-210).
- **Other hooks**: `client/src/features/home/data/identity.ts` (rename and photo),
  `client/src/features/home/data/talk.ts` (Turn on Talk, Apply, "Stop work and apply",
  and the retry note), `client/src/features/home/data/liveTask.ts:36-63` (the live "Now"
  line from the todo cache and node statuses), `client/src/features/home/data/usage.ts`,
  `client/src/features/home/data/skills.ts`, `client/src/features/home/data/profile.ts`,
  `client/src/features/home/approvals/data.ts`.

Requests Home sends (all over the main WebSocket, snake_case payloads):

| Purpose | Request types |
|---|---|
| Team | `list_employees`, `get_employee`, `get_employee_usage` |
| Hiring | `generate_employee_setup`, `cancel_employee_setup`, `hire_employee` |
| Control | `start_employee`, `pause_workflow`, `resume_workflow` (through `useWebSocketActions`), `enable_employee_talk`, `apply_employee_changes` (optionally `stop_work: true`) |
| Identity | `rename_employee`, `set_employee_photo` (after `POST /api/workspace/{workflow_id}/uploads`) |
| Teams and access | `plan_employee_team`, `give_employee_team`, `list_employee_access`, `decide_employee_access` |
| Settings | user settings read and save, the user-skill family (`create_user_skill`, `update_user_skill`, `delete_user_skill`, `get_skill_content`, `lookup_skill_metadata`), the credential catalogue |
| Delete | `DELETE /api/database/workflows/{id}` through `useAppStore.deleteWorkflow` |

`client/src/contexts/WebSocketContext.tsx`):

| Wire key | Routing | Effect |

#### 5.3 Runs and streaming

- A message the deployed chat trigger will answer starts a **chat run**; one live run per
  session (the lane). Send becomes Stop while it lives; Esc anywhere in the pane stops it
  (`client/src/features/chat/ChatPane.tsx:285-294`).
- Run events arrive only for subscribed sessions (`chat_subscribe`,
  `client/src/features/chat/data/runs.ts:65`), carry `seq` and `hub_epoch`, and are folded
  by `client/src/lib/agui/reduceRun.ts` into `chatRunStore` once per animation frame;
  gaps trigger a snapshot resync. Only the agent answering the owner streams text; tool
  calls show as steps with plugin-provided labels; reasoning never streams.
- Text renders block by block while streaming
  (`client/src/features/chat/markdown/ReplyMarkdown.tsx:78-90`,
  `client/src/features/chat/markdown/blocks.ts`) with a pulsing caret dot
  (`client/src/index.css:659-679`).
- The steps disclosure (`client/src/features/chat/turns/StepsDisclosure.tsx:52-87`) is a
  pill reading "Working…" (open, shimmering) and then "Worked for 12s · 3 steps",
  expanding to a step list with a spinner, tick, cross or dash.

3-minute cap; the recording is uploaded, turned into text by `transcribe_audio` (which
deletes it) and appended to the draft. The microphone shows only when
`dictation_status` reports a speech provider with a key
(`client/src/features/chat/data/chatContext.ts:77-104`). This is speech-to-text into the
box, not a voice message.

#### 5.7 Generated UI

`client/src/features/chat/turns/GeneratedUiBlock.tsx` lazily renders a reply's `ui`
parts with json-render (`client/src/features/chat/genui/ChatUi.tsx`), re-sanitised
(`client/src/features/chat/genui/prepare.ts`, `client/src/lib/jsonRender/`), revealed
element by element while live, and drawn from a fixed catalogue of twelve components
(`client/src/features/chat/genui/catalog.ts`: Stack, Row, Card, SlotPicker, Select,
Toggle, TextField, Text, StatGrid, BarChart, Callout, Button). Owner edits sync through
`chat_ui_state` (after 300 ms idle and on hide); a button press becomes
`send_chat_message{ui_event}` and an `action` turn. The server mirrors the catalogue in
`server/config/chat_genui_catalog.json`. Development builds add an Inspect view. The Home
setup screen uses a separate catalogue (`client/src/features/home/genui/`, private behind
its `index.ts`).

#### 5.8 Approval cards

`client/src/features/chat/approval/ApprovalCard.tsx` (theme hook `chat-approval`):
recipient, channel, the message as it will go, Discard / Edit / Send; after Send a
countdown with Undo (5 s), then Sending and Sent (or failed with Try again behind a
confirmation); a discarded draft can be restored while its window lasts; "Sends when you
resume" for a paused employee's gate. Cards sit on the reply that made them, or after
the thread for drafts from the employee's own work
(`client/src/features/chat/approval/StandaloneApprovals.tsx`). Ctrl/Cmd+Enter sends the
newest pending draft (`client/src/features/chat/ChatPane.tsx:276-294`). The Ask first
chip changes the live rule (`set_ask_first`).

#### 5.9 Branches, versions and feedback

Edit opens in place (`client/src/features/chat/turns/UserEditBox.tsx`) and starts a new
branch; Try again regenerates the latest answer; `‹ 1 / 2 ›` switches versions
(`client/src/features/chat/turns/VersionStepper.tsx`); the server decides what is
`editable` and refuses with codes such as `revision_conflict` or `cannot_rewind`, told in
the host's words (`client/src/features/chat/turns/runCopy.ts`). The reply bar
(`client/src/features/chat/turns/ReplyActions.tsx:51-97`) offers Copy, Good and Bad
(toggle buttons with `aria-pressed`; the toast says the employee will see the rating
next time), Try again, the version stepper and the time.

#### 5.10 Sources, follow-ups and artifacts

- `[n]` citations become chips; cited sources list under the answer as host-and-title
  chips (`client/src/features/chat/turns/SourceChips.tsx:19-63`); numbering is per
  conversation.
- Up to three follow-up suggestions show under the latest finished answer
  (`client/src/features/chat/turns/FollowUps.tsx`).
- A document the run wrote on its Canvas shows as a card with title, kind and version
  (`client/src/features/chat/turns/ArtifactCard.tsx:12-37`); Open asks the host to show
  it (Home: the Workspace's Canvas tab at that version; Dev: the Canvas dock).

#### 5.11 Keyboard map (fixed, not configurable)

Cmd/Ctrl+K focuses the box on Home
(`client/src/features/home/employee/EmployeeChat.tsx:126-134`); Esc stops a running
answer; Ctrl/Cmd+Enter sends the newest draft; ArrowUp edits the last message; Enter and
Tab pick a slash command; Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+D switches modes; the editor has its own command
palette (`client/src/components/ui/CommandPalette.tsx`) and F2 rename on the canvas.

#### 5.12 Chat wire summary

Requests: `send_chat_message`, `get_chat_messages`, `chat_subscribe`, `chat_unsubscribe`,
`get_chat_run`, `stop_chat_run`, `chat_ui_state`, `edit_chat_message`,
`regenerate_chat_reply`, `switch_chat_branch`, `set_chat_feedback`, `get_chat_context`,
`clear_chat_messages`, `list_approvals`, `get_approvals`, `decide_approval`,
`get_ask_first`, `set_ask_first`, `canvas_version`, `dictation_status`,
`transcribe_audio`; HTTP uploads and file reads under `/api/workspace/{workflow_id}/`.
Message rows carry `id`, `role`, `kind` (`text`, `report`, `action`, `notice`), `text`,
`timestamp`, `run_key`, `run_id`, `parent_id`, `status`, `attachments`, `parts` (`ui`,
`artifacts`, `approvals`, `sources`, `followups`), `siblings`, `editable`, `feedback`
and an optional `run` summary (`client/src/features/chat/data/schemas.ts:69-111`). There
is no author field beyond `role`, no reaction field and no read marker.

### 6. Workspace dock, Settings and hiring (context)

- **Workspace** (`client/src/features/home/workspace/WorkspaceDock.tsx`): one employee at
  a time (the one last opened, else the first). Browser uses the shared live viewer
  (`client/src/components/browser/BrowserWorkspace.tsx`: binary JPEG frames over
  `/ws/browser`, Take control / Hand back, Help in browser); Canvas shows the employee's
  board (`client/src/features/home/workspace/WorkspaceCanvas.tsx`, lazy); Mobile shows
  the managed local Android emulator (`client/src/components/mobile/MobileWorkspace.tsx`).
  At 1100px and wider it pushes the page; below, it overlays with `shadow-dock`. Its
  resize separator is mouse-drag only
  (`client/src/features/home/workspace/WorkspaceDock.tsx:218-228`); Expand
  (`client/src/features/home/workspace/WorkspaceDock.tsx:67`) is the non-drag size
  control. Full view (`client/src/components/workspace/FullView.tsx`) uses native
  fullscreen.
- **Settings**: Profile (names, role, preferences, timezone, `memory_across_chats`,
  `prefer_local_ai`, appearance), Billing (tasks this month and the employee count only,
  `client/src/features/home/settings/BillingTab.tsx:27-42`), Skills (the library plus a
  Discover folder), Connectors (the shared `CredentialsBrowser`: every provider in
  `server/config/credential_providers.json`, grouped by `consumer_category`: `ai`,
  `developer` including `claude_code` and `codex_cli`, `messages`, `organize`, `devices`
  including `browser` and `android_remote`, `research`, `business`, `language`), Plugins
  (starter bundles), and App access.
- **Hiring**: describe a job, an LLM drafts a json-render setup screen, and Hire builds,
  validates, saves and starts the workflow. The builder always creates an `aiAgent` whose
  provider and model come from the model that wrote the setup screen
  (`server/services/employees/builder.py:766-781`); Start moves an agent on an unusable
  provider to the owner's current model (`server/services/employees/start.py:50-82`).

`design_handoff_opencompany_home/` (gitignored; the 2026-10-03 export according to the
repo's notes) holds `chat/README.md`, `tokens/chat.css` and

The handoff's top-level `README.md:18` still says "This is not a chat product", which
predates the chat screen. The repo's tokens win where values differ
(`docs-internal/normal_mode.md:26-30`).

### 8. Backend facts that shape any Noodle-like UX

- **A chat session is one saved workflow.** `server/services/chat/access.py:48-61`
  refuses a session id that names no saved workflow and any socket whose principal is not
  the workflow's owner; only the editor's `"default"` session has no workflow.
- **One persona, one answering agent.** The talk line is chatTrigger, then an agent, then
  Reply in Chat (`docs-internal/normal_mode.md:538-578`). Teammates in a team work
  through Task Manager behind the lead and never post into the thread
  (`docs-internal/employee_teams.md`, `docs-internal/agent_teams.md`); the live work card
  can name the member per step (`client/src/features/home/employee/EmployeeWork.tsx:72`).
- **Conversation lifetime follows the workflow.** The thread is stamped with the
  generation; a Reset clears it with the agent's Context; "New conversation" clears it;
  threads are per workflow, not per user (`docs-internal/normal_mode.md`, Known gaps).
- **The message box follows control state.** Running, starting or resuming sends;
  paused or pausing queues one message; anything else has no box
  (`client/src/features/home/data/presentation.ts:134-151`, the `delivery` of
  `send_chat_message`).
- **One live run per session.** A second send answers `run_in_progress`; edit,
  regenerate and switch are refused while a run holds the lane.
- **Summaries carry no conversation metadata.** `list_employees` returns status, task,
  `done_today`, `pending_approvals`, apps, control, `hired_at` and workspace nodes, but no
  last message, last activity time or unread count. Searches of `server/services/` for
  unread, last-message, reaction and presence terms, and of `server/services/chat/` for
  read and seen timestamps, found no such fields (the only "delivered" hits are chat
  notes' `delivered_at` and the run failure code `not_delivered`).
- **Multi-user is authentication without isolation.** `AUTH_MODE=multi` shares one
  workflow and credential store (`CLAUDE.md`, Authentication System).
- **Desktop shell.** `desktop/src/main/index.ts:159-163` allows same-origin
  `window.open` and sends every other URL to the OS browser, so a same-origin pop-out
  window is possible in the Electron app; the SPA has no route or state model for one.
